definition_zh: 不相容的；不兼容的；合不来的
definition_en: unable to exist or work together because of basic differences, or unable to get along with another person
core_image: 两块拼图：边缘形状不合，无论怎样按压都拼不进去
scene: 两位室友作息完全不同，说话方式也相反。Looking back, the two flatmates were simply incompatible.
sceneCN: 这里 incompatible 是「合不来的」（第 2 个义项：性格或相处方式不合）；句意：回头看，这两位室友本就合不来。

pos.zh: 不相容的；不兼容的；合不来的

derivatives.zh: 由 incompatible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「不合；不兼容」
去掉否定前缀 in- 的形式，义为「相容的；兼容的」
由 compatible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「相容性；兼容性」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「相容地」

senses.title: Unable to exist or work together
senses.definition: so different in their basic nature that two things cannot exist or work together
senses.definitionCN: 在基本性质上差别太大，以致两样东西无法同时存在或配合工作
senses.example: Nuclear power is seen by some as incompatible with a green economy.
senses.exampleCN: 有人认为核电与绿色经济不相容。
senses.why: The prefix in- negates the Latin base meaning able to suffer with, so incompatible describes two pieces that cannot share one place.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了拉丁词根「能够与之共同承受」的意思，所以这个词描述的是无法同处一块地方的两个部件。

senses.title: Cannot get along as people
senses.definition: of two people, unable to live or work happily together because their temperaments clash
senses.definitionCN: 指两个人因性格冲突而无法愉快地相处或共事
senses.example: The two managers were incompatible and clashed at every meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 两位经理合不来，每次开会都会起冲突。
senses.why: When the two pieces that must meet are people instead of objects, the failed fit becomes a clash of temperaments.
senses.whyCN: 当必须拼合的两个人而非物件时，「拼不上」就变成了性情上的冲突。

senses.title: Cannot be used together
senses.definition: of a machine, program, or device, unable to operate properly with another system
senses.definitionCN: 指机器、程序或设备无法与另一系统正常配合运行
senses.example: This old printer is incompatible with the new computer.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧打印机与新电脑不兼容。
senses.why: Technology borrows the word for parts that refuse to link, giving the everyday sense of a device that will not speak the same language.
senses.whyCN: 技术领域借用了这个词，专指拒绝连接起来的部件，于是有了「设备之间语言不通」的日常含义。

senses.title: Parts that cannot be combined
senses.definition: of aims, beliefs, or proposals, so opposed that they cannot both be held or achieved
senses.definitionCN: 指目标、观念或提案彼此对立，无法同时持有或同时实现
senses.example: The boss wants faster delivery, which is incompatible with his smaller budget.
senses.exampleCN: 老板想要更快的交付，这与他更小的预算互相矛盾。
senses.why: Ideas behave like puzzle pieces too: two aims that cannot sit side by side are marked by the same missing fit.
senses.whyCN: 观念也像拼图块：两个无法并排放置的目标，同样被标记为「拼不上」。

senses.title: Medical mismatch
senses.definition: of blood, tissue, or drugs, unable to be introduced into the body without causing a harmful reaction
senses.definitionCN: 指血液、组织或药物进入身体后会引起有害反应
senses.example: The donor organ was found to be incompatible with the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 人们发现供体器官与这位病人不相容。
senses.why: In medicine the word names a physical refusal to merge, the most literal version of two shapes that will not lock together.
senses.whyCN: 医学里这个词指身体层面拒绝融合，是「两块形状锁不上」最字面的版本。

intro.en: Incompatible joins Latin in-, not, to a Medieval Latin adjective meaning able to suffer together, from the verb pati, to suffer.
intro.cn: incompatible 由拉丁语否定前缀 in-（不）加一个中世纪拉丁语形容词构成，该形容词意为「能够共同承受」，源自动词 pati（忍受、承受）。

items.en: The verb pati means to suffer or endure, and gives the passive participle passus.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 pati 意为「忍受、承受」，其被动分词是 passus。

items.en: The adjective passibilis, able to suffer, is built from passus and the suffix -bilis.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语由 passus 加后缀 -bilis 构成形容词 passibilis，意为「能够承受的」。

items.en: Compatibilis is formed with the prefix com-, together, meaning able to suffer or bear things together.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语加前缀 com-（共同）构成 compatibilis，意为「能够共同承受的」。

items.en: The negated form incompatibilis adds in- to the same adjective.
items.cn: 否定形式 incompatibilis 在同一形容词前加 in-。

items.en: English borrows the word around the sixteenth century, first of temperaments and later of devices and systems.
items.cn: 英语约在十六世纪借用此词，起初用于性情，后来扩展到设备与系统。

note.en: Incompatible lives in the com- family of compatible, and its core idea of parts that will not fit brings it near hostile, conflicting, and mismatched.
note.cn: incompatible 属于 compatible 这一带前缀 com- 的词族，其「部件拼不上」的核心概念让它靠近 hostile、conflicting 与 mismatched。

entries.definitionCN: 相容的；兼容的

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be combined
entries.definitionCN: 不相容地

entries.definition: the state of not being able to work together
entries.definitionCN: 不合；不兼容

entries.definition: unfriendly or opposed to something
entries.definitionCN: 敌对的；不友善的

entries.definition: in disagreement with each other
entries.definitionCN: 相互冲突的

entries.definition: badly paired, so that the parts do not suit each other
entries.definitionCN: 搭配不当的

normalIntro.en: Incompatible is the negative of compatible, and the Latin inside means able to bear things together, so the word pictures things that cannot be carried in one basket.
normalIntro.cn: incompatible 是 compatible 的否定，里面藏着的拉丁义是「能够共同承受」，所以这个词描绘的是装不进同一只篮子的东西。

normal.en: The pattern incompatible with is the standard construction, as in a habit that is incompatible with health.
normal.cn: incompatible with 是标准搭配模式，例如「与健康不相容的习惯」。

normal.en: Mutually incompatible marks two things that exclude each other.
normal.cn: mutually incompatible 标记两样互相排斥的东西。

normal.en: The noun is incompatibility, formed with -ity.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 incompatibility，由后缀 -ity 构成。

normal.en: Software and hardware that will not talk to each other are called incompatible.
normal.cn: 彼此无法沟通的软件与硬件被称作「不兼容」。

normal.en: Compare compatible and its cousin incompatible: one fits, the other never will.
normal.cn: 对比 compatible 与它的否定形式：一个能拼上，另一个永远拼不上。

abstract.en: Picture two puzzle pieces with the wrong grooves pressed together.
abstract.cn: 想象两块凹槽不对的拼图被用力按在一起。

abstract.en: Imagine two people who speak the same language but never understand each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人说着同一种语言，却始终听不懂对方。

abstract.en: Think of a charger whose plug is a size too big for the socket.
abstract.cn: 想象一个插头比插座大一号的充电器。

examples.en: The film was praised for showing that two strong beliefs can be incompatible.
examples.cn: 这部影片因展示出两种坚定信念可以互不相容而受到称赞。

examples.en: Her perfectionism was incompatible with the fast pace of the newsroom.
examples.cn: 她的完美主义与新闻编辑室的快节奏根本不协调。

examples.en: Check the manual before installing software that may be incompatible.
examples.cn: 安装可能不兼容的软件前，请先看说明书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + com + pat + ible」——想「配」到一起却怎么都不合拍，就是不相容。这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pati（承受）→ 晚期拉丁语 passibilis（能够承受的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 compatibilis（能够共同承受的）→ incompatibilis（不能共同承受）→ 英语 incompatible，核心义「无法共同存在」。

sensesIntro.en: Incompatible begins with objects or conditions that cannot share a space, then moves to people who clash, then to devices, clashing aims, and finally to a body that rejects a graft.
sensesIntro.cn: incompatible 先指无法共处一处的物件或条件，再指互相冲突的人，然后依次指设备、矛盾的目标，最后指身体对移植物的排斥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pieces with edges that will not lock together.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块边缘锁不在一起的构件。

branches.en: The basic sense is a failure to coexist at all.
branches.cn: 基本义项指根本无法共存。

branches.en: People who clash turn the failed fit into personal conflict.
branches.cn: 互相冲突的人把「拼不上」变成人际矛盾。

branches.en: Devices that will not talk form the technical sense.
branches.cn: 无法沟通的设备构成技术含义。

branches.en: Aims that cannot both be met are incompatible in an abstract way.
branches.cn: 无法同时实现的目标以抽象方式互不相容。

branches.en: A physical refusal to merge and a biological rejection both mark things that cannot be combined.
branches.cn: 物理上的拒绝拼合与生物上的排斥，都标记着无法组合在一起的东西。

intro.en: Incompatible is a negated Latin adjective whose second half comes from pati, to suffer, linking it to patience and passive.
intro.cn: incompatible 是一个否定的拉丁语形容词，后半部分来自 pati（承受），因此与 patience、passive 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati means to suffer or endure; com- adds together, in- adds not.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati 意为忍受、承受；前缀 com- 加「共同」，前缀 in- 加「不」。

items.example: Pati is the deepest root of the word.
items.exampleCN: pati 是这个单词最底层的词根。

items.example: Passus is the participle that supplies the stem.
items.exampleCN: passus 是提供词干的分词。

items.example: The suffix -bilis builds passibilis.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -bilis 构成 passibilis。

items.example: The prefix com- marks shared bearing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 com- 标记共同承受。

items.example: Compatibilis is the direct ancestor of compatible.
items.exampleCN: compatibilis 是 compatible 的直接祖先。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the whole adjective.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定整个形容词。

items.example: Compatible is the positive partner of the word.
items.exampleCN: compatible 是这个词的肯定搭档。

items.example: The suffix -ity turns incompatible into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把 incompatible 变成名词。

items.meaning: the state of not being compatible
items.example: Incompatibility is the abstract noun form.
items.exampleCN: incompatibility 是抽象名词形式。

items.example: Patience shares the Latin root pati.
items.exampleCN: patience 共享拉丁词根 pati。

definition_zh: 不能胜任的；无能的；不合格的；不具资格的
definition_en: lacking the skill or ability needed for a job, or not legally able to act in a particular role
core_image: 一个人站在梯子前，伸手也够不到最后一级踏板
scene: 那位新经理答应得好好的，却从不跟进任何事情。A few weeks later, even his closest ally called him incompetent.
sceneCN: 这里 incompetent 是「不能胜任的」（第 1 个义项：做某事所缺的能力）；句意：几周之后，连他最亲近的盟友都称他不能胜任。

pos.zh: 不能胜任的；无能的；不合格的
无能的人；不称职者

collocations.zh: 一个完全不能胜任的老师

derivatives.zh: 由 incompetent 换名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「无能；不称职」
由后缀 -ency 构成的名词，义为「无能力」，多用于法律语境
去掉否定前缀 in- 的形式，义为「有能力的；称职的」
由 competent 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「能力；胜任力」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「称职地；胜任地」

senses.title: Lacking skill for a job
senses.definition: not having the skill or knowledge needed to do a job properly
senses.definitionCN: 缺少把一件事做好的技能或知识
senses.example: The committee blamed an incompetent manager for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把延误归咎于一位不称职的经理。
senses.why: In- says not, and the Latin base is the participle of a verb meaning to aim at, so the person cannot reach the mark expected of the role.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 表示「不」，词根是动词「瞄准、使劲够到」的分词，因此这人够不到岗位所要求的目标。

senses.title: Unfit for a particular duty
senses.titleCN: 不适合担任某职；不合格
senses.definition: not suitable or fit for a particular post because the required qualities are missing
senses.definitionCN: 因为缺少所需素质而不适合担任某个职务
senses.example: Doctors judged him incompetent to drive after the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 医生判定他在受伤后不适合开车。
senses.why: The same missing mark is applied to a specific duty rather than general work, so the word becomes a judgement about fitness for a role.
senses.whyCN: 同样是够不到目标，但这里针对的是某项具体职责而非一般工作，于是这个词变成对任职资格的判定。

senses.title: Not legally qualified
senses.titleCN: （法律上）无资格的；无行为能力的
senses.definition: in law, not having the legal power or qualification to act or to give evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上不具有采取行动或作证的法定资格或行为能力
senses.example: The court held that the witness was incompetent to testify.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定该证人不具备作证资格。
senses.why: Law makes the inability formal: the person lacks the legal standing rather than the talent, and the court supplies the mark.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这种「不够」正式化：缺的不是才能而是法定资格，「目标」由法院来设定。

senses.title: A worthless person
senses.definition: used as a noun, an insulting word for a person who cannot do things well
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时对做不好事情的人的贬称
senses.example: The critics dismissed him as a political incompetent.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把他贬为一个政治上无能的人。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun of abuse, turning the failed reach for the mark into a label stuck on the whole person.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作带贬义的名词，把「够不到目标」浓缩成贴在整个的人身上的标签。

intro.en: Incompetent joins Latin in-, not, to competent, from competere, to strive after something together or to be suitable.
intro.cn: incompetent 由拉丁语否定前缀 in-（不）加 competent 构成，后者出自 competere，意为「共同争取」或「相称、合适」。

items.en: Competere joins com-, together, and petere, to seek or aim at, giving the idea of aiming at the same thing.
items.cn: competere 由 com-（共同）与 petere（寻求、瞄准）合成，义为「共同瞄准同一目标」。

items.en: Competens, the present participle, means suitable or having a claim to something.
items.cn: 现在分词 competens 意为「相称的、有资格主张的」。

items.en: French competent and its negated partner carry the sense of fitting for a purpose.
items.cn: 法语 competent 及其否定形式都表示「适合某一目的」。

items.en: English adopts competent in the sense of suitable or sufficient, and the negated form soon means unfit for a post.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 competent，义为「合适的、足够的」，其否定形式很快表示「不适合担任某职」。

items.en: Modern English adds the legal sense of lacking capacity and the noun use as a term of abuse.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了法律上缺乏行为能力的含义，以及作为贬称的名词用法。

note.en: Incompetent is the negative of competent within the competing family, and it sits close to words that judge ability or rank fitness.
note.cn: incompetent 是 competent 这一 competing 词族中的否定形式，它与那些评判能力或任职资格的词相邻。

entries.definition: having enough skill to do a job well
entries.definitionCN: 有能力的；称职的

entries.definition: lack of skill or ability
entries.definitionCN: 无能；不称职

entries.definition: to try to win against others
entries.definitionCN: 竞争；比赛

entries.definition: not having the training or licence required
entries.definitionCN: 不合格的；无资格的

entries.definition: clumsy and lacking skill in what one does
entries.definitionCN: 无能的；笨拙的

entries.definition: not suitable for a purpose or role
entries.definitionCN: 不适合的

normalIntro.en: Incompetent keeps the shape of competent, which names someone who can aim at the mark and reach it; in- cancels that reach.
normalIntro.cn: incompetent 保留了 competent 的形状，后者指能瞄准目标并击中的人；前缀 in- 把这记「够到」取消掉了。

normal.en: In- is the Latin prefix for not, so incompetent is the plain negative of competent.
normal.cn: in- 是拉丁语表示「不」的前缀，所以 incompetent 就是 competent 的简单否定。

normal.en: The Latin verb competere joins com-, meaning together, with petere, meaning to aim at.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 competere 由 com-（共同）与 petere（瞄准）合成。

normal.en: The noun is incompetence, and the legal form is incompetency.
normal.cn: 名词是 incompetence，法律语境中作 incompetency。

normal.en: The adjective is followed by at, as in someone incompetent at math.
normal.cn: 这个形容词后面常接 at，例如「在数学上无能」。

normal.en: Compare competent: competent says the aim is reached, incompetent says the aim is missed.
normal.cn: 对比 competent：一个是打中目标，一个是打不中目标。

abstract.en: Picture a worker holding tools that are all too large for his hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一名工人握着的工具全都比他的大一号。

abstract.en: Imagine a ladder missing its last step, stopping the climber just below the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子缺了最后一级，让人停在顶端下方。

abstract.en: Think of a signature on a document that the law refuses to accept.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件上的签名被法律拒绝承认。

examples.en: The report found the hospital management incompetent and careless.
examples.cn: 报告认定医院管理层既不称职又粗心。

examples.en: Making a mistake does not by itself make a worker incompetent.
examples.cn: 犯一次错本身并不能说明一个员工不能胜任。

examples.en: The defence lawyer argued that the child was incompetent to testify.
examples.cn: 辩护律师主张这名儿童不具备作证资格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + com + pet + ent」——连小事都「陪」不上、跟不上节拍，就是不能胜任。这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 com-（共同）+ petere（寻求、瞄准）→ competere（共同争取、相称）→ 英法语 competent（合适的、称职的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 的 incompetent（不足以胜任）。

sensesIntro.en: Incompetent first marks a person who cannot reach the standard a job demands, then narrows to fitness for a single duty, then to legal capacity, and finally becomes a noun of abuse.
sensesIntro.cn: incompetent 先标记达不到工作要求的人，再收窄为对某一项职责是否适合，然后指法定资格，最后转为贬义名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose outstretched arm cannot reach the top rung of the ladder.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人伸手也够不到梯子的最高一级。

branches.en: Ordinary lack of skill is the main everyday sense.
branches.cn: 普通意义上的能力不足，是日常主要义项。

branches.en: Fitness for a particular duty is the narrower form.
branches.cn: 对某项具体职责的适合度是更窄的形式。

branches.en: Legal capacity replaces talent with formal standing.
branches.cn: 法定资格用正式身份替代了才能。

branches.en: As a noun the word becomes a label of contempt.
branches.cn: 作名词时这个词成了蔑视性的标签。

branches.en: At work the judgement that someone is incompetent often turns into a judgement that the person is unfit to hold the post.
branches.cn: 在工作中，判断某人能力不足，往往会变成判断此人不适合担任该职位。

intro.en: Incompetent is built on competence and compete, whose Latin base petere, to aim, also feeds petition and appetite.
intro.cn: incompetent 建立在 competence 与 compete 之上，其拉丁词根 petere（瞄准）还孕育了 petition 与 appetite。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere means to seek or aim at; com- joins two aims into one contest, and in- cancels the ability to reach it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 petere 意为寻求、瞄准；前缀 com- 把两个志向并成一场竞争，前缀 in- 取消够到的能力。

items.example: Petere gives the aiming image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: petere 提供了这个词背后的「瞄准」意象。

items.example: The prefix com- joins two seekers into one contest.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 com- 把两个寻求者并成一场竞争。

items.meaning: to strive together, to be suitable
items.example: Competere carries both the contest and the fit.
items.exampleCN: competere 同时承载「竞争」与「相称」两层含义。

items.example: Competens is the participle that becomes the adjective.
items.exampleCN: competens 是演变为形容词的分词。

items.example: The prefix in- removes the suitability.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 去掉了「相称」。

items.example: Competent is the positive partner of the word.
items.exampleCN: competent 是这个词的肯定搭档。

items.example: The suffix -ent marks the person or thing acting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 标记执行动作的人或物。

items.example: The suffix -ence forms incompetence.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 构成 incompetence。

items.example: Incompetence is the abstract noun form.
items.exampleCN: incompetence 是抽象名词形式。

items.example: Compete shares the same Latin base.
items.exampleCN: compete 共享同一拉丁基础。

definition_zh: 难以置信的；无法想象的；绝无可能的；难以言状的；不可容许的
definition_en: too strange, unlikely, or extreme for the mind to grasp or accept
core_image: 一片云雾飘到人面前，人伸手去接，却怎么也拢不住
scene: 那天天空压得极低，云团像倒挂的山峦悬在头顶，老人抬头看了一整晚。The scale of the storm overhead was inconceivable to everyone on the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 inconceivable 是「难以置信、无法想象」（第 1 个义项：某事物离奇到头脑接不住）；句意：头顶那场风暴的规模对山丘上的每个人来说都难以想象。

pos.zh: 难以想象的；难以置信的；绝无可能的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，表示「令人难以置信地」
去掉否定前缀 in-，表示「可以想象的；可能的」
基础动词：构想；孕育

senses.title: Too strange for the mind to accept
senses.definition: so surprising or unlikely that the mind cannot really take it in
senses.definitionCN: 某事离奇、不合常理，以至于人几乎无法接受或想象
senses.example: The speed of the rescue was inconceivable to the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这次营救的速度让村民们难以置信。
senses.why: Latin in- negates and conceivere means to take in or grasp; the mind literally cannot take the thing in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示否定，conceivere 意为「接纳、把握」，合起来就是头脑没法把这件事装进去、想不通。

senses.title: Impossible in practice
senses.definition: extremely unlikely ever to happen or be achieved
senses.definitionCN: 在现实中几乎根本不可能发生或实现
senses.example: Raising the fee without public support would be inconceivable.
senses.exampleCN: 没有公众支持就提高收费，是不可想象的。
senses.why: If the mind cannot form a picture of a result, the practical chance of it looks like zero.
senses.whyCN: 既然脑海里连结果的样子都拼不出来，现实中的成功概率自然被看成零。

senses.title: A thing of pure imagination
senses.definition: existing only as a vague fancy that could never come true
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于空泛的想象里、根本不可能成真
senses.example: Without funding the whole plan was a sweet but inconceivable dream.
senses.exampleCN: 没有资金支撑，整个计划只是一个美好的空想。
senses.why: The oldest sense keeps the root image: the mind builds ideas, and some ideas stay outside what the world can ever produce.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项保留了词根意象：头脑会构建观念，而有些观念永远落在现实能产出之物以外，所以只能算空想。

senses.title: Beyond what words can render
senses.definition: too extreme or vast for speech to capture
senses.definitionCN: 程度过于极端或宏大，语言根本无法如实描述
senses.example: The vastness of the open desert is almost inconceivable.
senses.exampleCN: 空旷沙漠的辽阔几乎难以言状。
senses.why: What cannot be grasped by the mind also resists exact description; the shock itself outruns ordinary words.
senses.whyCN: 头脑都把握不住的东西，语言也很难如实描摹；震撼本身跑到了日常词汇的前头。

senses.title: Not allowed by a system of rules
senses.titleCN: 不合规矩的；不被容许的
senses.definition: outside what a body of rules or customs permits
senses.definitionCN: 超出某一套规则或惯例所允许的范围
senses.example: A teacher acting like that would be inconceivable in this school.
senses.exampleCN: 在这所学校里，老师那样做是不可想象的。
senses.why: Shared norms train the mind: when a step breaks them, the mind rejects it before any careful reasoning begins.
senses.whyCN: 共同规范先给头脑定了框架，一旦某一步越出框架，头脑在细想之前就已经把它否掉了。

senses.title: Picture, faintly, and still not believe
senses.titleCN: 很难相信，尽管并非完全不可能
senses.definition: hard to picture and believe, even when it is remotely possible
senses.definitionCN: 即便只是万一可能，也依旧难以想象、难以置信
senses.example: It seems inconceivable, yet the records show the trade did once happen.
senses.exampleCN: 这看起来令人难以相信，但记录显示这笔交易确实发生过。
senses.why: The word keeps one foot in capability: what is conceivable at the far margin is not yet unthinkable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终留着一只脚在「能够把握」那边：即便处在能想到的最边缘，也还没有变成完全不可想的东西。

intro.en: Inconceivable is in- plus Latin concipere, whose root capere means to seize or take, the same root that gives capture and capacity.
intro.cn: inconceivable 由否定前缀 in- 与拉丁语 concipere 构成，词根 capere 意为「抓住、拿取」，capture、capacity 都出自同一词根。

items.en: A reconstructed root kap- means to grasp or hold.
items.cn: 重构词根 kap- 意为抓住、握住，属推论所得。

items.en: The verb capere means to take or seize.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 capere 意为拿取、抓住。

items.en: Com plus capere gives concipere, to take together, and so to form a thought or to become pregnant.
items.cn: com 加 capere 构成 concipere，意为「一起收拢」，引申为构想、受孕（conceive 的「怀孕」义即由此而来）。

items.en: Conceivable enters English as capable of being thought.
items.cn: conceivable 进入英语后表示「能够设想的」。

items.en: The adjective conceivabil is recorded in Middle English, and in- later makes it negative.
items.cn: 中古英语时期已见形容词 conceivabil，后加否定前缀 in- 构成反义。

items.en: From the 17th century the negative form covers unlikely, impossible, and unacceptably odd.
items.cn: 这一否定形式后来逐步覆盖「难以置信、绝无可能、不合情理」等义。

note.en: Inconceivable belongs to the capere family of words, close to unimaginable, impossible, and implausible in meaning.
note.cn: inconceivable 属于 capere 词根家族，意义上与「无法想象」「绝无可能」「难以置信」几个词相邻。

entries.definition: able to be imagined or believed
entries.definitionCN: 可以想象的；可信的（去掉否定前缀的正向形式）

entries.definition: to form an idea or to become pregnant
entries.definitionCN: 构想；怀孕

entries.definition: in a way that is impossible to imagine
entries.definitionCN: 难以想象地

entries.definition: too extreme or strange to be imagined
entries.definitionCN: 难以想象的；不可设想的

entries.definition: not able to happen or be done
entries.definitionCN: 不可能的；办不到的

entries.definition: hard to believe
entries.definitionCN: 难以置信的；不太可信的

normalIntro.en: Break the word as in plus conceive plus able: nothing can be conceived, so nothing can be accepted.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 in 加 conceive 加 able：conceive 意为构想、孕育，in 否定，-able 表示能够，合起来就是「无法构想」。

normal.en: The base verb conceive means to form a thought, and its root means to take hold.
normal.cn: 基础动词 conceive 意为构想，其词根意为抓住、握住。

normal.en: Conceivable means able to be imagined, so in front closes that door.
normal.cn: conceivable 意为可以想象的，前面加上 in 就把这扇门关上。

normal.en: The common pattern is it seems inconceivable that, followed by a clause.
normal.cn: 常见句型是「it seems inconceivable that」后接从句，表示简直无法想象。

normal.en: The word is often softened with almost or virtually.
normal.cn: 这个词常被 almost 或 virtually 软化语气，表示「几乎」不可能。

normal.en: As a negative extreme, the word pairs with unlikely and impossible on a scale from chance to zero chance.
normal.cn: 作为否定程度上的极端，它与 unlikely、impossible 连用，构成从「不大可能」到「毫无可能」的尺度。

abstract.en: Picture yourself trying to catch a cloud with bare hands.
abstract.cn: 想象你伸出空手去接一朵云，怎么都拢不住。

abstract.en: Picture a thought knocking on a closed door that never opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头敲门，门却始终不开。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that floats for years without ever touching soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子漂了很多年，始终没有落到土里。

examples.en: It is inconceivable that the family survived on so little money for ten years.
examples.cn: 这家人靠那么少的钱撑了十年，简直无法想象。

examples.en: To the young climbers, the old photograph of the peak was inconceivable scenery.
examples.cn: 对年轻登山者来说，那张山顶的老照片是难以想象的景色。

examples.en: A modern city without clean water would be inconceivable.
examples.cn: 一座没有清洁用水的现代城市是不可想象的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬肯思唯宝」——硬着头皮也不肯想过这件宝物会存在，表示难以置信；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ concipere（com 一起 + capere 抓住 → 收拢、构想）+ -able（能够）→ 英语 inconceivable，字面意思是「抓不住、构想不出来的」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts from the mind failing to take something in, then widens to practical impossibility, to fancy, to speech, to rules, and to a faint doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「头脑装不进去」出发，依次延伸到现实中的不可能、纯属空想、语言难以描述、规矩不容许，最后到达「很想不信却还不能彻底排除」的余地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reaching for a cloud, and the hand closes on nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手去接一朵云，手一合却什么也没抓住。

branches.en: Mind meets a thing it cannot accept; surprise dominates.
branches.cn: 头脑遇上接不住的事物，惊讶感占上风。

branches.en: What the mind cannot hold is judged unlikely, then nearly ruled out.
branches.cn: 头脑握不住的事先被判定为不大可能，再被几乎排除。

branches.en: Fancy and speech are the corners where the image drifts away.
branches.cn: 空想与言说，是意象渐渐散去的两个边角。

branches.en: Norms harden the same reaction into a rule of what is allowed.
branches.cn: 规范把这同一种反应固化成「允不允许」的规矩。

branches.en: Everyday speech uses the negative extreme to stress how remarkable, shocking, or impossible a thing is.
branches.cn: 日常用语借这个否定极端，强调某事有多了不起、多惊人或多不可能。

intro.en: Inconceivable is a prefixed, suffixed form of the Latin root capere, with conceit, concept, and conception in its wider family.
intro.cn: inconceivable 是拉丁词根 capere 的前缀兼后缀形式，更大的词族里还有 conceit、concept、conception。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere means to take, and concipere means to take together or to conceive in the mind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取，concipere 意为「一起收拢」，即构想。

items.example: The prefix in- makes inconceivable mean not able to be conceived.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 让 inconceivable 表示「无法构想」。

items.example: The root capere supplies the image of taking hold.
items.exampleCN: 词根 capere 提供「抓住」的意象。

items.example: Concipere gives the verb conceive.
items.exampleCN: concipere 演变为动词 conceive。

items.example: She could conceive of a fairer system.
items.exampleCN: 她能构想出一个更公平的制度。

items.example: The suffix -able forms conceivable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 conceivable。

items.example: Every conceivable option was tested.
items.exampleCN: 凡是能想到的方案都试过了。

items.example: The costs were inconceivably high.
items.exampleCN: 成本高得难以想象。

items.example: Concept shares the root capere.
items.exampleCN: concept 与它共享词根 capere。

items.example: Conception adds a noun ending.
items.exampleCN: conception 加了名词后缀。

definition_zh: 不协调；不相称；前后矛盾；格格不入的事物
definition_en: the quality of being strange or unsuitable because parts do not fit together
core_image: 一块形状古怪的拼图按进缺口，边缘歪着，怎么也推不平
scene: 拼图只剩最后一块，形状却和缺口对不上，边角始终翘着。The single carved piece was an incongruity in the smooth wooden box.
sceneCN: 这里 incongruity 是「不协调、不相称的事」（第 1 个义项：各部分对不上）；句意：那块雕花木片放进光滑的木盒里，显得格格不入。

pos.zh: 不协调；不相称；不一致；格格不入的事物

derivatives.zh: 加 -ous 构成形容词，表示「不协调的；格格不入的」
去掉否定前缀 in-，表示「一致性；协调」
由 in- 加拉丁分词 congruent 构成，表示「不一致的」

senses.title: The state of not fitting together
senses.definition: a state in which parts fail to fit or work together
senses.definitionCN: 各部分彼此不配套、无法协调一致的状况
senses.example: There is a clear incongruity between the report and the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的内容与数据之间明显不协调。
senses.why: Latin in- denies and congruere means to run together or agree, so the noun names something whose parts will not run in step.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示否定，congruere 意为「一起走、彼此相符」，这个名词指的就是各部分走不到一块儿的状态。

senses.title: Failing to match in logic
senses.definition: a failure of two statements, plans, or beliefs to agree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个说法、计划或信念彼此对不上、相互打架
senses.example: The reviewers spotted an incongruity in the second chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 审稿人发现了第二章里的前后矛盾。
senses.why: When two claims do not agree, the mismatch becomes a visible flaw in the argument.
senses.whyCN: 两个说法彼此不符时，这种不配套就在论证里显形，成为看得见的漏洞。

senses.title: Not matching the surroundings
senses.definition: a thing or person that does not go well with its setting
senses.definitionCN: 某物或某人与所处环境不搭调、格格不入
senses.example: The plastic chair was an incongruity in the old stone hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那把塑料椅子摆进古老的石头大厅里，显得格格不入。
senses.why: A setting has its own style, and anything that clashes with that style stands out as an odd note.
senses.whyCN: 场所有自己的风格，凡是与这种风格相冲的东西，都会像跑调的杂音一样跳出来。

senses.title: Comic absurdity of the mismatched
senses.definition: the strange or funny effect produced by things that do not belong together
senses.definitionCN: 本不该放在一起的东西并置时，产生的怪异或滑稽效果
senses.example: The film gets its humour from the incongruity of a butler in a war zone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的幽默来自「管家出现在战区」这种不搭调。
senses.why: Humour often fires when the mind predicts one setting and meets its opposite in the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 头脑先按某种情境做预测，却在同一幅画面里撞见它的反面，笑点往往就此产生。

senses.title: The fact of being simply wrong
senses.definition: the quality of being unreasonable and therefore out of place
senses.definitionCN: 某事物本身不合情理，因而显得不当
senses.example: Few people noticed the incongruity of praising thrift in an advertising campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有人注意到，在广告宣传里赞美节俭是多么不当。
senses.why: The older sense stretches the image from physical fit to logical fit, so any flaw of reasoning can be called an incongruity.
senses.whyCN: 较早的用法把「拼不上」从实物延展到道理上，于是推理里任何对不上的地方都能叫不协调。

intro.en: Incongruity is Latin in- plus congruere, from con- together and the ancient root gru-, whose meaning is traced through to agree and to run together.
intro.cn: incongruity 由拉丁语 in- 与 congruere 构成；congruere 由 con-（一起）和古词根 gru- 组成，一般解释为与我们「相符」、与我们相应地行动。

items.en: A reconstructed element gru- is thought to mean to agree or to run with.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构成分 gru- 表示「相符、结伴而行」。

items.en: Congruere means to come together, to agree, or to fit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 congruere 意为走到一起、相符、合得上。

items.en: The negative form incongruus means not agreeing or not fitting.
items.cn: 否定形式 incongruus 意为不相符、不合拍。

items.en: Incongruitie enters English through French, first naming things that do not fit.
items.cn: 经法语进入英语的 incongruitie 记录于十五世纪，最初指对不上的事物。

items.en: The noun extends to logical and stylistic disagreement.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐扩展到逻辑上的前后矛盾与文理上的不协调。

items.en: Modern use keeps both the logical sense and the comic sense of things that clash.
items.cn: 现代用法既保留逻辑矛盾，也保留错配产生的荒诞滑稽感。

note.en: Incongruity is the noun beside incongruous and incongruent, and it overlaps in meaning with inconsistency and mismatch.
note.cn: incongruity 是形容词 incongruous、incongruent 对应的名词，意义上与「不一致」「不般配」几个词重叠。

entries.definition: not matching or agreeing
entries.definitionCN: 不一致的；不相配的

entries.definition: the quality of fitting together
entries.definitionCN: 协调；一致（去掉否定前缀的对应名词）

entries.definition: in agreement or of the same size and shape
entries.definitionCN: 一致的；全等的

entries.definition: a lack of agreement between parts
entries.definitionCN: 不一致；前后矛盾

entries.definition: a difference that should not be there
entries.definitionCN: 差异；不符之处

entries.definition: a statement that seems to contradict itself
entries.definitionCN: 悖论；看似矛盾的说法

normalIntro.en: Incongruity is in- plus congruity, and congruitas comes from Latin congruus, so the word means the absence of fit.
normalIntro.cn: incongruity 由 in- 加 congruity 构成，而 congruitas 来自拉丁语 congruus，因此这个词的意思就是「合不上」。

normal.en: The base verb congruere means to agree or to fit.
normal.cn: 基础动词 congruere 意为相符、合得上。

normal.en: The noun takes the -itas ending that becomes English -ity.
normal.cn: 这个名词带 -itas 结尾，到英语里就成了 -ity。

normal.en: The adjective incongruous is the partner form.
normal.cn: 与之配套的形容词形式是 incongruous。

normal.en: The standard frame is an incongruity between one thing and another.
normal.cn: 常见框架是 an incongruity between 某物和某物。

normal.en: Literary critics use the word for the deliberate clash of comic effect.
normal.cn: 文学评论里常用这个词指刻意制造笑料的冲撞。

abstract.en: Picture a metal gear dropped into a wooden clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚金属齿轮掉进了木头钟表里。

abstract.en: Picture two people dancing to different tunes in one room.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在同一个房间里各跳各的曲子。

abstract.en: Picture a palace built of two clashing styles of stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一座宫殿用两种互相打架的石材砌成。

examples.en: The incongruity of the scene made everyone laugh.
examples.cn: 那场景中的不搭调让所有人都笑了。

examples.en: Budget cuts sit in stark incongruity with the promises of growth.
examples.cn: 预算削减与增长承诺之间形成鲜明的反差。

examples.en: Critics pointed to the incongruity of a luxury hotel beside the slums.
examples.cn: 批评者指出，把豪华酒店建在贫民区旁边实在格格不入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬康雇」——硬要雇一个格格不入的人，处处不协调；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ congruere（con 一起 + 古词根 gru- 相符）→ incongruus → 法语 incongruite → 英语 incongruity，字面意思「合不上」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with physical misfit, then spreads to logic, to setting, to the comic effect of mismatch, and to what is simply unreasonable.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「实物拼不上」出发，扩展到逻辑上的不符、与环境的不搭调、错配带来的滑稽感，以及本身就不合理的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece pressed into the wrong gap, still crooked.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块拼图硬按进错的缺口，边角依旧翘着。

branches.en: Two parts refuse to line up; this is the abstract core sense.
branches.cn: 两个部分对不齐，这是最抽象的核心义项。

branches.en: The same misfit moves inside an argument or a plan.
branches.cn: 同样的合不上挪进了论证或计划内部。

branches.en: A thing misfits its surroundings, and people notice the clash.
branches.cn: 一件东西与周围环境不合，别人一眼就看见。

branches.en: A visible clash can switch from jarring to funny.
branches.cn: 看得见的不协调可以从刺眼转成好笑。

branches.en: What does not fit can also simply be wrong or improper.
branches.cn: 对不上的东西，也可以直接就是错的或不当的。

intro.en: Incongruity is built from the negative prefix in-, the Latin verb congruere, and the noun ending -ity.
intro.cn: incongruity 由否定前缀 in-、拉丁语动词 congruere 与名词后缀 -ity 三部分拼成。

latinIntro.en: Latin congruere means to come together or agree, and incongruus means not agreeing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 congruere 意为走到一起、相符，incongruus 意为不相符。

items.example: The prefix in- turns congruity into incongruity.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 congruity 变成 incongruity。

items.example: Congruere gives the whole family.
items.exampleCN: congruere 衍生出整个词族。

items.example: Incongruus is the negative Latin form.

items.example: The adjective incongruous describes a clashing scene.

items.example: The adjective incongruent is used in geometry.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 incongruent 常用于几何学。

items.example: Two congruent triangles have the same shape and size.

items.example: Congruous describes what fits well.

definition_zh: 不协调的；格格不入的；不一致的；荒谬的；不恰当的
definition_en: strange and unsuitable because something does not fit its surroundings or its logic
core_image: 一身晚礼服的人踩进泥泞的田埂，鞋子和庄稼互相对视
scene: 乡间婚礼的宴席上有人端着香槟走过稻草堆，来宾们忍不住多看了几眼。The city suit looked incongruous among the straw hats and dusty boots.
sceneCN: 这里 incongruous 是「不协调、格格不入」（第 1 个义项：与周围环境不搭）；句意：那身城里西装在一群草帽和沾满灰尘的靴子中间显得格格不入。

pos.zh: 不协调的；格格不入的；不一致的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ity 构成名词，表示「不协调；格格不入」
加 -ly 构成副词，表示「不协调地」
去掉否定前缀 in-，表示「协调的；合适的」

senses.title: Not fitting the surroundings
senses.definition: strange and unsuitable because it does not fit its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 因与周围环境不搭调而显得奇怪、不合适
senses.example: A loud laugh seemed incongruous in the quiet library.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的图书馆里，一声大笑显得格格不入。
senses.why: Latin in- denies and congruere means to agree or fit, so the adjective marks a thing that will not fall in line with its setting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示否定，congruere 意为相符、合拍，这个形容词指的就是不肯与环境合拍的东西。

senses.title: Clashing in style or tone
senses.definition: having a style or tone that clashes with what stands next to it
senses.definitionCN: 风格或语气与旁边的部分相互冲突
senses.example: Colourful posters look incongruous on the grey stone walls.
senses.exampleCN: 花花绿绿的海报贴在灰色石墙上显得很不协调。
senses.why: The clash is a matter of colour, register, or taste rather than of physical space.
senses.whyCN: 这种冲撞出在色彩、语体或审美趣味上，而非物理空间上。

senses.title: Not agreeing in logic
senses.definition: failing to agree with another fact or statement
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事实或说法对不上、相互矛盾
senses.example: His cheerful account was incongruous with the gloomy data.
senses.exampleCN: 他乐观的说法与惨淡的数据相互矛盾。
senses.why: When two things cannot stand together, the adjective moves from space to argument.
senses.whyCN: 当两样东西没法并列共处时，这个形容词就从空间挪到了论证里。

senses.title: Comically mismatched
senses.titleCN: 荒诞滑稽的；错觉得好笑的
senses.definition: making a strange or funny impression through an odd combination
senses.definitionCN: 因组合怪异而给人荒诞、滑稽的印象
senses.example: The image of a clown at a funeral was grotesque yet incongruous.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼上出现小丑的画面既古怪又荒诞。
senses.why: The clash of expectations can tip from jarring into funny.
senses.whyCN: 期待落空的冲撞，有时会从刺眼滑向好笑。

senses.title: Improper for the occasion
senses.definition: unacceptable or unsuitable for a given occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在特定场合显得不合适、不容许
senses.example: Jokes about illness are incongruous at a charity dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 在慈善晚宴上拿疾病开玩笑很不合时宜。
senses.why: The stronger, older sense adds judgement: not merely odd, but wrong for the occasion.
senses.whyCN: 更强也更早的义项加上了评判：不只是奇怪，而是在这个场合不对。

intro.en: Incongruous is the Latin in- plus congruus, literally not agreeing, from congruere, to come together or fit.
intro.cn: incongruous 由拉丁语 in- 与 congruus 构成，字面意为「不相符」，源自 congruere（走到一起、合得上）。

items.en: A reconstructed element gru- is thought to mean to agree or run with.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构成分 gru- 表示「相符、结伴而行」。

items.en: Congruere, from con- together, means to fit or agree.
items.cn: congruere 由 con-（一起）构成，意为合得上、相符。

items.en: Incongruus denies that fit: not agreeing.
items.cn: incongruus 否定这种合拍，意为不相符。

items.en: The adjective incongruous is recorded in English in the early seventeenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 incongruous 以这一形式见于十七世纪初的英语（更早的拼写为 incongruent）。

items.en: The word is used for clashes of style and for comic effect.
items.cn: 此后它常用来描写风格上的冲突与滑稽效果。

items.en: Modern use covers setting, logic, propriety, and humour.
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖环境、逻辑、得体与幽默四个方面。

note.en: Incongruous is the adjective in the congruere family, framing the same idea that keeps incongruity as a noun.
note.cn: incongruous 是 congruere 词族里的形容词，它与作名词的 incongruity 表达同一个概念，只是词性不同。

entries.definitionCN: 不协调；不相称（对应的名词形式）

entries.definition: not matching or agreeing
entries.definitionCN: 不一致的；不相配的（同根异形）

entries.definition: fitting or suitable

entries.definition: not suitable for the situation
entries.definitionCN: 格格不入；不得体

entries.definition: wildly unreasonable
entries.definitionCN: 荒谬的；荒唐的

entries.definition: containing parts that do not agree
entries.definitionCN: 不一致的；前后矛盾的

normalIntro.en: Incongruous is in- plus congruous, so it describes something that will not sit in agreement with what surrounds it.
normalIntro.cn: incongruous 由 in- 加 congruous 构成，用来描述没法与周围环境合拍的东西。

normal.en: The root congruere means to fit or agree.
normal.cn: 词根 congruere 意为合得上、相符。

normal.en: The adjective usually takes a contrast after with or in.
normal.cn: 这个形容词后常跟 with 或 in，引出形成对照的对象。

normal.en: It is common with sit, seem, strike someone as, and look.
normal.cn: 它常与 sit、seem、strike someone as、look 连用，表示看起来如何。

normal.en: The noun incongruity names the same clash, and incongruously is the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词 incongruity 指同一种冲突，副词是 incongruously。

normal.en: Compare consistent, which is the neutral neighbour in argument and planning.
normal.cn: 对比 consistent：它是论证与计划语境中语气中性的邻近词。

abstract.en: Picture a baseball cap on a marble statue.
abstract.cn: 想象给大理石雕像戴一顶棒球帽。

abstract.en: Picture a bright cartoon in a museum of old oil paintings.
abstract.cn: 想象把鲜艳的卡通画挂进古典油画馆。

abstract.en: Picture jogging shoes paired with a ball gown.
abstract.cn: 想象晚礼服配一双跑步鞋。

examples.en: The modern tower looks incongruous beside the medieval church.
examples.cn: 那座现代高塔立在中世纪教堂旁边显得格格不入。

examples.en: His cheerful voice was incongruous with the news he brought.
examples.cn: 他轻快的语气与带来的消息很不协调。

examples.en: Some critics found the jazz score incongruous with the tragic plot.
examples.cn: 一些评论者觉得爵士配乐与悲剧情节不相称。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬靠过」——硬要靠过去却总对不上，只能不协调地站着；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ congruus（相符的，源自 congruere：con 一起 + gru- 相符）+ -ous（形容词后缀）→ 英语 incongruous，字面意思「对不上」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts from physical misfit, then moves to clash of style, to logical disagreement, to comic effect, and finally to what is improper.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从实体的合不上出发，依次延伸到风格冲突、逻辑不符、滑稽效果，最后落到不合时宜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: formal dress stepping into a muddy field.
core.cn: 核心意象：一身正装踩进泥泞的田里。

branches.en: The essential sense: a thing that does not fit where it stands.
branches.cn: 最基本的义项：站在那儿就不合适的东西。

branches.en: The misfit is felt in colour, register, or taste.
branches.cn: 这种不合出现在色彩、语体或品味层面。

branches.en: The same word judges whether facts agree with one another.
branches.cn: 同一个词也用来判断几个事实彼此是否对得上。

branches.en: A clash can be enjoyed as absurd or funny.
branches.cn: 冲撞也可以被当成荒诞或好笑来欣赏。

branches.en: Not fitting easily escalates into not proper for the occasion.
branches.cn: 「不合」很容易升级为「在场合里不当」。

intro.en: Incongruous is built from in-, the Latin adjective congruus, and the adjective ending -ous, with incongruity and incongruously beside it.
intro.cn: incongruous 由 in-、拉丁形容词 congruus 与形容词后缀 -ous 拼成，旁边还有 incongruity 与 incongruously 两个同族词。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 congruus 意为相称、相符，动词 congruere 意为相符。

items.exampleCN: congruere 是源动词。

items.exampleCN: congruus 提供拉丁形容词部分。

definition_zh: 不显眼的；不引人注意的；不起眼的
definition_en: not easily seen or noticed, so that other people pay little attention to it
core_image: 一只灰扑扑的书包混在一排同样的书包中间
scene: 教室里几十个同样的书包挂在椅背上，其中一个朴素得很，谁也不会多看一眼。A plain grey bag hung among dozens of identical ones, inconspicuous enough that nobody noticed it.
sceneCN: 这里 inconspicuous 是「不显眼的、不引人注意的」（第 1 个义项：事物本身难以被看见或注意到）；句意：一个朴素的书包挂在几十个一样的书包中间，不起眼到没人注意到它。

pos.zh: 不显眼的；不引人注意的；不起眼的

collocations.zh: 不显眼的消费（隐形消费）

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不显眼地；不引人注意地」
基础词加 -ness 构成抽象名词，义为「不起眼的状态」
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的正面词，义为「显眼的；引人注目的」
由 conspicuous 加 -ness 构成，义为「显眼；引人注目」

senses.title: Not easily noticed physically
senses.definition: attracting little attention because of colour, size, or position
senses.definitionCN: 因颜色、大小或位置而不太吸引注意力
senses.example: She chose an inconspicuous coat for the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这次出行挑了一件不显眼的外套。
senses.why: The prefix in- reverses species, the look, so the word says a thing has no striking appearance for the eye to catch.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了「外观、样子」这层意思，所以这个词表示某物没有惹眼的外表可供眼睛捕捉。

senses.title: Deliberately blending in
senses.definition: acting or being styled so as not to stand out on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意让人或物不出众、不惹人注意
senses.example: He kept an inconspicuous pace behind the guide.
senses.exampleCN: 他不紧不慢地跟在向导身后，尽量不惹眼。
senses.why: From being literally unseen, the word moves to the human choice of staying unnoticed and thereby safe.
senses.whyCN: 从「字面上看不见」引申为人的主动选择：保持不被注意，从而安全稳妥。

senses.title: Minor and easy to miss
senses.definition: small or fine enough to be missed even when one is looking
senses.definitionCN: 很小或很细微，即使留心看也容易漏掉
senses.example: There was an inconspicuous crack near the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 画框旁边有一道很不显眼的裂纹。
senses.why: What the eye fails to catch is often simply tiny, so the word drifts from hidden to small in detail.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛抓不住的东西往往就是细小之物，于是词义从「隐蔽」滑向「细节微小」。

senses.title: Modest in style or design
senses.definition: plain in decoration or design so as not to draw the eye
senses.definitionCN: 装饰或设计朴素，不吸引目光
senses.example: The company uses inconspicuous fonts on its cards.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在名片上使用朴素而不张扬的字体。
senses.why: Colour and ornament are what make things conspicuous, so restraint in design is read as the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 颜色和装饰正是让人显眼的原因，因此设计上的克制也被看成同一件事。

senses.title: Slight and unremarkable in effect
senses.definition: present but of little visible effect or importance
senses.definitionCN: 存在但影响或重要性不明显
senses.example: The change produced an inconspicuous gain in speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改动带来的速度提升微乎其微。
senses.why: If a result escapes the eye, speakers extend the word from things to the size of their effects.
senses.whyCN: 既然结果逃过眼睛的察觉，说话者就把这个词从实物扩展到效果的大小。

intro.en: Inconspicuous is formed in English from the prefix in- and the Latin-descended adjective conspicuous, with in- here meaning not.
intro.cn: inconspicuous 是在英语中由前缀 in- 加源自拉丁语的形容词 conspicuous 构成，这里的 in- 意为「不」。

items.en: Conspicuus means visible or open to view, from conspicere, to look at.
items.cn: consicere 一系的 conspicuus 意为「可见的、看得见的」，源于 conspicere（观看）。

items.en: Conspicere is com- together plus specere, to look.
items.cn: conspicere 由 com-（一起）与 specere（看）合成。

items.en: Conspicuous enters English from Latin with the sense clearly visible.
items.cn: conspicuous 在十六世纪由拉丁语进入英语，意为「清楚可见」。

items.en: The negative prefix in- is added to conspicuous, giving inconspicuous.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 被加到 conspicuous 之前，形成 inconspicuous。

items.en: The word widens from hard to see to modest, slight, and deliberately unshowy.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义从「难以看见」扩展到「朴素、轻微、刻意不张扬」。

note.en: Inconspicuous sits at the negative edge of a family built on Latin specere, to look, and stands opposite conspicuous.
note.cn: inconspicuous 处在以拉丁语 specere（看）为词根的词族的否定一端，与 conspicuous 互为反面。

entries.definition: clearly visible and attracting attention
entries.definitionCN: 显眼的；引人注目的（与目标词只差否定前缀 in-）

entries.definition: in a way that is hard to notice
entries.definitionCN: 不显眼地；不引人注意地

entries.definition: the quality of not being noticed
entries.definitionCN: 不起眼的状态

entries.definition: too slight or subtle to be noticed
entries.definitionCN: 察觉不到的；不易注意到的

entries.definition: careful not to attract attention or cause embarrassment
entries.definitionCN: 谨慎的；不张扬的

entries.definition: not noticeable or pushy
entries.definitionCN: 不唐突的；不引人注目的

normalIntro.en: Inconspicuous is conspicuous with in- in front: the same visible look, now taken away.
normalIntro.cn: inconspicuous 就是在 conspicuous 前面加上 in-：同样的「看得见」，现在被拿走了。

normal.en: Drop the in- and you get conspicuous, which means highly visible.
normal.cn: 去掉 in- 就得到 conspicuous，意思是「非常醒目」。

normal.en: The shared root spec- means to look, so conspicuous things cry out to the eyes.
normal.cn: 共同的词根 spec- 意为「看」，所以 conspicuous 的东西直往眼睛里钻。

normal.en: Pair it with the adverb inconspicuously: do it in a way that nobody sees.
normal.cn: 记住副词 inconspicuously：以没人注意得到的方式去做。

normal.en: A person who stays inconspicuous keeps quiet, blends in, and draws no comment.
normal.cn: 保持 inconspicuous 的人安静、融入人群、不招评论。

normal.en: Compare the pair: conspicuous dress shouts, inconspicuous dress whispers.
normal.cn: 对比这一对词：conspicuous 的穿着在大喊，inconspicuous 的穿着在低语。

abstract.en: Picture a grey cat sleeping on a grey sofa, all but invisible.
abstract.cn: 想象一只灰猫睡在灰沙发上，几乎与背景融为一体。

abstract.en: Imagine slipping through a crowd without a single head turning.
abstract.cn: 想象你穿过人群，没有一颗脑袋转过来看你。

abstract.en: Think of a faint scratch on dark wood that only shows in strong light.
abstract.cn: 想想深色木头上那道浅痕，只有强光下才看得见。

examples.en: The path to the cottage was inconspicuous from the main road.
examples.cn: 通往小屋的小径从大路上看很不显眼。

examples.en: Witnesses said the suspect wore inconspicuous clothing.
examples.cn: 目击者说嫌疑人穿着毫不引人注意的衣服。

examples.en: A good assistant stays inconspicuous until called.
examples.cn: 好的助手在被叫到之前一直低调不显眼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因看四皮丢斯」——「因」为「看」不到（spec 意为看），就「丢」在了人群里；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 conspicere（一起观看）→ conspicuus（看得见的）→ 英语 conspicuous（显眼的）＋否定前缀 in- → inconspicuous，核心义「不惹眼」。

sensesIntro.en: Inconspicuous begins with things the eye cannot catch, deepens into the human choice of blending in, and finally fades to things that are small, plain, or slight.
sensesIntro.cn: inconspicuous 先指眼睛捕捉不到的事物，再深入为人的主动融入，最后淡化为「细小、朴素、轻微」的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one plain bag among a row of identical bags.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排同样的书包里那只朴素的书包。

branches.en: Something hard to see is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 难以看见的事物是字面义项。

branches.en: Choosing to blend in is the active personal sense.
branches.cn: 主动融入人群是主动的义项。

branches.en: Missing a detail and missing an effect both mean the change escapes the eye.
branches.cn: 漏看一个细节与感觉不到一个效果，都是变化逃过了眼睛。

branches.en: A plain design wins no attention by refusing colour and ornament.
branches.cn: 朴素的设计靠拒绝颜色与装饰来避免被注意。

branches.en: Both the pale coat and the faint crack owe their privacy to low contrast.
branches.cn: 浅色外套与浅淡裂纹都靠低对比度获得隐蔽性。

intro.en: Inconspicuous pairs the negative prefix in- with conspicuous, which goes back to Latin specere, to look.
intro.cn: inconspicuous 由否定前缀 in- 与 conspicuous 组合，后者可追溯到拉丁语 specere（看）。

latinIntro.en: Latin conspicere means to look at together, and conspicuus means open to view.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 conspicere 意为「一同观看」，conspicuus 意为「看得见的」。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把形容词的意思反过来。

items.example: Latin con- stands for together.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语前缀 con- 表示「一起」。

items.example: The root spec- means to look.
items.exampleCN: 词根 spec- 意为「看」。

items.example: Conspicere is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: conspicere 是源词。

items.example: Conspicuus gives the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: conspicuus 提供形容词词干。

items.example: Conspicuous is the positive form.
items.exampleCN: conspicuous 是肯定形式。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成这个形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inconspicuously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 inconspicuously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms inconspicuousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 inconspicuousness。

items.example: Inconspicuous is the negative form.
items.exampleCN: inconspicuous 是否定形式。

definition_zh: 错误地；不正确地；不恰当地
definition_en: in a way that is wrong, mistaken, or not according to fact or rule
core_image: 答题卡上本该打勾的方框被画上了叉
scene: 学生答完卷子后，把答案栏里本该打勾的方框错画成了叉。After finishing the paper, the student marked the answer box incorrectly with a cross instead of a tick.
sceneCN: 这里 incorrectly 是「错误地」（第 1 个义项：做法或说法不符合事实或标准）；句意：学生答完卷子后，在本该打勾的答案栏里错画成了叉。

pos.zh: 错误地；不正确地；不恰当地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「不正确的；错误的」
由 incorrect 加 -ness 构成，义为「不正确；错误」
去掉否定前缀 in- 的正面形式，义为「正确的」
correct 加 -ly 构成的正面副词，义为「正确地」

senses.title: In a wrong factual way
senses.definition: in a way that does not match the facts
senses.definitionCN: 以与事实不符的方式
senses.example: The form was filled in incorrectly.
senses.exampleCN: 表格被填错了。
senses.why: The adverb names the manner of an action, and in- plus correct says that manner does not line up with the truth.
senses.whyCN: 副词说明动作的方式，in- 加 correct 表示这种方式与事实对不上。

senses.title: Against a rule or standard
senses.definition: in a way that breaks an agreed rule, method, or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 以违反既定规则、方法或程序的方式
senses.example: The samples were stored incorrectly for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这些样本被不合规地存放了两周。
senses.why: Rules are treated as the corrected standard of a process, so breaking them is acting in the negative manner.
senses.whyCN: 规则被视为流程的「正确标准」，违反规则也就是以否定的方式行事。

senses.title: By mistake rather than intent
senses.definition: as a result of carelessness or a slip rather than on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 由于疏忽或失手而不是故意地
senses.example: She dialled the number incorrectly twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她两次都拨错了号码。
senses.why: Many wrong actions come from a moment of inattention, so the adverb also points at the slip, not the plan.
senses.whyCN: 许多错误动作源于一时的疏忽，所以这个副词也指向失手，而不是意图。

senses.title: Not understood correctly
senses.definition: in a way that misreads what someone meant
senses.definitionCN: 以误读他人本意的方式
senses.example: My words were quoted incorrectly in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 报告中引用我的话时有误。
senses.why: Reading a message wrongly is still a manner of receiving it, so the adverb extends to understanding.
senses.whyCN: 把信息读错也是一种「接收方式」，于是副词扩展到理解层面。

intro.en: Incorrectly is an English formation: the negative prefix in- plus Latin-derived correct, and the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: incorrectly 是英语自行构成的词：否定前缀 in- 加源自拉丁语的 correct，再加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Corrigere means to put right or to straighten, built from com- together and regere, to rule or guide.
items.cn: corrigere 意为「纠正、弄直」，由 com-（一起）与 regere（统治、引导）构成。

items.en: Correctus is the past participle with the sense set right.
items.cn: correctus 是过去分词，意为「被纠正的」。

items.en: Correct enters English with the sense in line with the rule.
items.cn: correct 在十四世纪进入英语，意为「合乎规则的」。

items.en: The prefix in- is added to correct, giving incorrect.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 加到 correct 之前，形成 incorrect。

items.en: The suffix -ly makes the adverb incorrectly.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 incorrectly。

note.en: Incorrectly is the manner adverb of the negative pair, standing opposite correctly.
note.cn: incorrectly 是这对正反词里的方式副词，与 correctly 相对。

entries.definition: wrong or not according to fact
entries.definitionCN: 不正确的；错误的

entries.definition: the state of being wrong
entries.definitionCN: 不正确的状态

entries.definition: in the right way
entries.definitionCN: 正确地（与目标词只差否定前缀）

entries.definition: in a mistaken or unfair way
entries.definitionCN: 错误地；冤枉地

entries.definition: by error of judgement
entries.definitionCN: 错误地；误以为地

entries.definition: in a way that is not acceptable or suitable
entries.definitionCN: 不恰当地；不合规矩地

normalIntro.en: Incorrectly is simply incorrect plus the adverb ending -ly, so it describes how something is done.
normalIntro.cn: incorrectly 就是 incorrect 加副词词尾 -ly，所以它描述「怎么做的」。

normal.en: The ending -ly marks adverbs, so incorrectly answers the question how.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 标记副词，所以 incorrectly 回答「如何」的问题。

normal.en: The prefix in- makes the negative jump, from correct to incorrect.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 完成否定的一跳：从 correct 到 incorrect。

normal.en: The root regere means to guide straight, so a correct answer follows the line.
normal.cn: 词根 regere 意为「引直」，所以正确答案是沿着直线走的。

normal.en: Use it with verbs: spell incorrectly, answer incorrectly, label incorrectly.
normal.cn: 把它和动词搭配：spell incorrectly、answer incorrectly、label incorrectly。

normal.en: Compare correctly: the pair differ by one prefix and one meaning.
normal.cn: 对比 correctly：这一对只差一个前缀，意思正好相反。

abstract.en: Picture a tick turned into a cross on the same little box.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个方框里，本该打勾的地方被画成了叉。

abstract.en: Imagine a ruler laid crooked across a page and the line drawn with it.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子在纸上摆歪了，笔就顺着歪尺画了出去。

abstract.en: Think of a clock set two minutes off and every train missed after that.
abstract.cn: 想想那只快了两分钟的钟，从此每趟车都错过。

examples.en: The address was printed incorrectly on the envelope.
examples.cn: 信封上的地址印错了。

examples.en: If you answer incorrectly, the machine sounds a low note.
examples.cn: 如果你答错，机器会发出一个低音。

examples.en: The medication was stored incorrectly and lost its strength.
examples.cn: 药物存放不当，失去了效力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因科瑞特力」——「因」为「科」目细节没顾好、费了「力」，结果还是做错；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 regere（引导、弄直）→ corrigere（纠正）→ correctus（被纠正的）→ 英语 correct → ＋否定前缀 in- → incorrect → ＋后缀 -ly → incorrectly，核心义「偏离正确」。

sensesIntro.en: Incorrectly starts by naming a factually wrong manner, then spreads to breaking rules, to careless slips, and finally to messages received wrongly.
sensesIntro.cn: incorrectly 先指与事实不符的做法，再扩展到违反规则、疏忽失手，最后到对信息理解有误。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tick replaced by a cross on the same answer box.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该打勾的方框被画上了叉。

branches.en: Factually wrong manner is the central sense.
branches.cn: 与事实不符的做法是核心义项。

branches.en: Breaking a rule is wrong manner applied to a method.
branches.cn: 违反规则是把错误方式用于流程。

branches.en: A slip explains how a wrong manner often happens.
branches.cn: 疏忽解释了错误方式常常如何发生。

branches.en: Misreading a message is a wrong manner of listening.
branches.cn: 误读信息是「听」这种动作的错误方式。

branches.en: A mislabelled sample is both factually and procedurally wrong.
branches.cn: 贴错标签的样本在事实与程序两方面都错了。

intro.en: Incorrectly stacks three pieces: the prefix in-, the Latin-derived root correct, and the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: incorrectly 由三块拼成：前缀 in-、源自拉丁语的 correct 词干，以及英语副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin regere means to guide straight, and corrigere means to set right.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regere 意为「引直」，corrigere 意为「纠正」。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the base.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 使词根转为否定。

items.example: Latin con- strengthens the verb.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语前缀 con- 加强动词语气。

items.example: The root reg- means to guide straight.
items.exampleCN: 词根 reg- 意为「引直」。

items.example: Regere supplies the root idea of straightness.
items.exampleCN: regere 提供「直」的词根含义。

items.example: Corrigere is the direct ancestor verb.
items.exampleCN: corrigere 是直接祖先动词。

items.example: Correct enters English from Latin.
items.exampleCN: correct 由拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: Incorrect is correct with the prefix in-.
items.exampleCN: incorrect 是 correct 加上前缀 in-。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Incorrectly modifies the verb in the sentence.
items.exampleCN: incorrectly 在句中修饰动词。

definition_zh: 增长；增量；增加额；（加在工资上的）定期加薪
definition_en: a small amount by which something increases, or the act of increasing
core_image: 楼梯上一级一级往上抬的小台阶
scene: 每天存进储钱罐一点零钱，罐子里的分量就一点点往上长。A little loose change went into the jar each day, so its increment kept climbing.
sceneCN: 这里 increment 是「增长；增量」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度增加的那一小部分）；句意：每天往罐子里放进一点零钱，罐里的分量就一点点往上增长。

pos.zh: 增长；增量；增加额

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -al 构成形容词，义为「逐步的；渐进的」
incremental 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「以渐进方式地」
同根异形词，义为「增加；增长」
同根 cresc- 相关的近义词，义为「逐渐积累的增长」

senses.title: An amount added
senses.definition: a small amount by which a quantity or value goes up
senses.definitionCN: 数量或价值增加的那一小部分
senses.example: Each increment added two hundred to the total.
senses.exampleCN: 每增加一次，总数就多出两百。
senses.why: The Latin root of growth is cut into a countable piece, so the word names the visible step rather than the whole rise.
senses.whyCN: 「增长」这个拉丁词根被切成了可计数的一块，所以这个词命名的是看得见的一级，而不是整段上升。

senses.title: A regular wage rise
senses.definition: an automatic regular increase in wages as years pass
senses.definitionCN: 随工龄按固定周期自动增加的工资
senses.example: Staff receive an annual increment in April.
senses.exampleCN: 员工每年四月获得一次定期加薪。
senses.why: Salary rises come in fixed steps, so the countable step sense becomes the name of a pay raise itself.
senses.whyCN: 薪资上涨是按固定档位来的，于是「计数的一块」就成了加薪这件事的名称。

senses.title: A fixed step in a scale
senses.definition: one of the equal steps into which a scale or series is divided
senses.definitionCN: 刻度或序列被划分出的相等的一段
senses.example: The dial moves in increments of five degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 旋钮以五度为一级跳动。
senses.why: A ladder is nothing but its steps, so a measured scale is described by its repeated equal increments.
senses.whyCN: 梯子就是一级级的台阶，所以有刻度的量程也用它重复相等的「级」来描述。

senses.title: A small change in a stored value
senses.definition: a single addition made to a stored number in a computer or counter
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或计数器里对一个数所做的一次增加
senses.example: The counter takes an increment each time the door opens.
senses.exampleCN: 门每开一次，计数器就取一次自增。
senses.why: Electronic counters take one step at a time, so the technical sense is the same physical step made invisible.
senses.whyCN: 电子计数器一次只走一步，所以技术义项就是同一个台阶被变得看不见而已。

senses.title: The process of increasing
senses.definition: the act or process of growing in size, amount, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在尺寸、数量或程度上变大的动作或过程
senses.example: The increment of the herd was slow but steady.
senses.exampleCN: 畜群的增长缓慢而稳定。
senses.why: Repeated single steps, taken together, become the ongoing movement of growth that the word can also name.
senses.whyCN: 一次次单独的台阶累加起来，就成了这个词同样可以指称的持续生长过程。

intro.en: Increment comes from Latin incrementum, a growth or increase, built on the root cresc-, to grow.
intro.cn: increment 来自拉丁语 incrementum（生长、增加），建立在词根 cresc-（生长）之上。

items.en: Crescere means to grow, to come into being, and to increase.
items.cn: crescere 意为「生长、出现、增长」。

items.en: Incrementum is the noun for growth, the act of growing, or that by which something grows.
items.cn: incrementum 是表示「生长、增长」，或「使其增长之物」的名词。

items.en: Increment enters English from Latin with the sense increase or growth.
items.cn: increment 在十五世纪由拉丁语进入英语，意为「增长」。

items.en: The word develops the countable sense of a fixed step or amount added at a time.
items.cn: 十九世纪前后发展出可数义：一次加入的固定一步或一定数量。

items.en: Computing and payroll extend it to automatic rises in a number or a salary.
items.cn: 现代的计算机与薪金用法把它扩展到数值或工资的自动递增。

note.en: Increment belongs to the Latin family of growth around crescere, alongside increase and the adjective incremental.
note.cn: increment 属于以拉丁语 crescere（生长）为核心的「增长」词族，与 increase、incremental 同族。

entries.definition: happening in small steps
entries.definitionCN: 逐步的；渐进的

entries.definition: in small steps over time
entries.definitionCN: 以渐进方式地

entries.definition: to become larger in amount
entries.definitionCN: 增加；增长

entries.definition: a person or thing added
entries.definitionCN: 增加的人或物

entries.definition: an increase in amount or level
entries.definitionCN: 上升；增长

entries.definition: something added to improve or complete
entries.definitionCN: 补充物；增补

normalIntro.en: Increment is the countable step of growth: the small bit that is added each time something goes up.
normalIntro.cn: increment 是增长的「可数台阶」：每上去一点，就加上来的那一小块。

normal.en: The root cresc- also lives in increase, so growth is the shared thread.
normal.cn: 词根 cresc- 也出现在 increase 里，生长是它们共同的线索。

normal.en: Add -al and you get incremental, meaning taking small steps.
normal.cn: 加上 -al 就是 incremental，意为「一小步一小步的」。

normal.en: In pay, an increment is the yearly automatic rise.
normal.cn: 在薪资语境里，increment 指每年自动的那次加薪。

normal.en: In instruments, phrases such as increments of five are a set step size.
normal.cn: 在仪器语境里，increments of five 这类说法表示固定的步长。

normal.en: Compare the pair: increase is the whole climb, increment is one stair.
normal.cn: 对比这一对：increase 是整段攀升，increment 是一级台阶。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where every step raises you the same small height.
abstract.cn: 想象一道每级都抬高同样高度的小台阶。

abstract.en: Imagine a savings jar whose level ticks up one coin at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个储钱罐，刻度一枚硬币一枚硬币地上升。

abstract.en: Think of a counter on a door that clicks plus one with every visitor.
abstract.cn: 想想门上的计数器，每来一位客人就咔嗒加一。

examples.en: Each increment of ten degrees made the room warmer.
examples.cn: 每调高十度，房间就暖和一些。

examples.en: Teachers receive an increment for every extra year of service.
examples.cn: 教师每多一年服务期就获得一次加薪。

examples.en: The governor moves in increments of a quarter of a turn.
examples.cn: 调速器以四分之一圈为一级移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克瑞门特」——「因」为每次多「克」一点、多迈一个「门」槛，数额就涨了一截；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 crescere（生长）→ incrementum（生长；增长之物）→ 英语 increment，核心义「一次加出来的那一小级」。

sensesIntro.en: Increment starts as an amount added, then becomes a fixed pay rise and a fixed step on a scale, moves into stored numbers, and finally covers the whole process of growing.
sensesIntro.cn: increment 先指加上去的那一部分，再固定为定期加薪与刻度上的一级，走进存储的数值，最后覆盖整个增长过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small stair rising above the one before it.
core.cn: 核心意象：比下一级略高一节的小台阶。

branches.en: The amount added is the basic countable sense.
branches.cn: 加上的数量是最基本的可数义项。

branches.en: A wage rise and a dial step are both a fixed equal increment.
branches.cn: 加薪与旋钮的一级是同一种固定等距的增量。

branches.en: A counter step is the same stair, hidden inside a machine.
branches.cn: 计数器的自增是同一种台阶，只是藏进了机器里。

branches.en: Many single steps add up to the process of growth.
branches.cn: 众多单独的台阶累加起来就是增长过程。

branches.en: Both a small addition and a regular step depend on repetition.
branches.cn: 小的增加量与规则的步长都依赖重复发生。

intro.en: Increment is built on the Latin root cresc-, to grow, with the Latin noun ending -ment marking the result of growth.
intro.cn: increment 建立在拉丁语词根 cresc-（生长）之上，拉丁名词词尾 -ment 标记生长的结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere means to grow, and incrementum means growth or that by which something grows.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere 意为「生长」，incrementum 意为「生长」或「使其增长之物」。

items.example: The root cresc- carries the idea of growth.
items.exampleCN: 词根 cresc- 携带生长的含义。

items.example: Crescere is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: crescere 是基础动词。

items.example: Incrementum is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: incrementum 是直接来源。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: The suffix -ment marks the result of growing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 标记生长的结果。

items.example: Increment enters English from Latin.
items.exampleCN: increment 由拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: The suffix -al forms incremental.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 incremental。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms incrementally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 incrementally。

items.example: Incremental describes step by step change.
items.exampleCN: incremental 描述一小步一小步的变化。

definition_zh: 使显得有罪；归罪于；牵连（他人）
definition_en: to make someone appear guilty of a crime or of some wrong doing
core_image: 一件落在被告座位上的东西，把罪名压到那个人身上
scene: 法庭上出示的一份文件，让原本否认的被告显得有了罪。The document shown in court began to incriminate the defendant.
sceneCN: 这里 incriminate 是「使某人显得有罪」（第 1 个义项：把罪名加到某人身上），法庭里出示的文件正是让人看起来有罪的证据；句意：法庭上出示的那份文件开始让被告显得有罪。

pos.zh: 使显得有罪；归罪于；牵连

collocations.zh: 罪证；能使人有罪的证据

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「归罪；连累」
由词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「使人有罪的」
self 与词根合成的名词，义为「自证其罪」

senses.title: To make someone look guilty
senses.definition: to make a person seem guilty of a crime or of doing something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 使某人看起来犯了罪或做了错事
senses.example: Two witnesses were called to incriminate the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 两名证人被传唤来证明司机有罪。
senses.why: The Latin noun crimen means an accusation or a charge, and the prefix in- puts that charge onto a person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 crimen 意为「指控、罪名」，前缀 in- 把这项指控按到某个人身上，于是词义就是「使某人显得有罪」。

senses.title: To involve another person in guilt
senses.definition: to involve another person in a crime or in a serious mistake
senses.definitionCN: 把另一个人牵连进犯罪或严重过错之中
senses.example: He refused to incriminate his brother during questioning.
senses.exampleCN: 他在接受讯问时拒绝牵连自己的兄弟。
senses.why: Because the charge is thrown onto a target, the verb easily widens to dragging a second person into the same blame.
senses.whyCN: 既然罪名是被投到某个对象身上的，这个动词自然就扩展到把第二个人一起拖进同一份罪责。

senses.title: To show guilt through evidence
senses.definition: to cause evidence or words to point to the guilt of a person
senses.definitionCN: 使证据或话语指向某人的罪行
senses.example: A note in his own handwriting incriminated him.
senses.exampleCN: 一张他亲笔写的字条证明他有罪。
senses.why: The object shifts from the person to the thing, so the evidence itself becomes the accuser.
senses.whyCN: 动作对象从人转到物，于是证据本身变成了指控者，这正是法律文本里常见的用法。

senses.title: To say something against oneself
senses.titleCN: 说出不利于自己（自证其罪）
senses.definition: to say or write something that could be used as evidence against yourself
senses.definitionCN: 说出或写下可能被用来对付自己的话
senses.example: You have the right to remain silent rather than incriminate yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 你有权保持沉默，而不必说出对自己不利的话。
senses.why: When the target is the speaker, the charge lands on the person who is speaking.
senses.whyCN: 当动作对象就是说话人自己时，罪名便落到说话人头上，于是形成「自证其罪」这一法律用语。

senses.title: To wrongly cause a charge
senses.definition: to cause someone to be suspected of a crime they did not commit
senses.definitionCN: 使并未犯罪的人受到犯罪嫌疑
senses.example: The stolen goods had been planted to incriminate an innocent person.
senses.exampleCN: 那些赃物是被栽种下来的，为的是诬陷一个无辜的人。
senses.why: Nothing in the verb says the charge is true, so it can also describe a false accusation.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词本身并不保证指控属实，因此它也能描述虚假的控告，也就是「诬陷」。

senses.title: To make something damaging look suspicious
senses.definition: to make a thing, a place, or a detail look suspicious and damaging
senses.definitionCN: 使某物、某个地点或细节显得可疑而成为不利把柄
senses.example: The muddy boots incriminated the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 那双沾泥的靴子让空屋子显出了可疑之处。
senses.why: The legal charge loosens into any detail that points at hidden guilt.
senses.whyCN: 法律的指控被松动成任何指向隐藏罪责的细节，于是这个词可以形容物件与场面。

intro.en: Incriminate comes from the Latin verb incriminare, built on the noun crimen, an accusation or charge.
intro.cn: incriminate 来自拉丁语动词 incriminare，它由名词 crimen（指控、罪名）构成。

items.en: Crimen means an accusation, a charge, or a crime.
items.cn: crimen 意为指控、罪名或罪行。

items.en: Incriminare means to charge someone with a crime.
items.cn: incriminare 意为控告某人犯罪。

items.en: The verb passes through later Latin and French forms before English.
items.cn: 这个词经晚期拉丁语与法语形式再进入英语。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the middle of the third century of English print and soon belongs to law.
items.cn: 这个动词在十八世纪中叶首次见于英语书面记录，并很快成为法律用语。

items.en: The legal noun incrimination takes its place beside the verb.
items.cn: 十九世纪，法律名词 incrimination 开始与这个动词并立。

items.en: The phrase right against self-incrimination enters constitutional language.
items.cn: 现代英语中，「反对自证其罪的权利」进入宪法语言。

note.en: Incriminate is the verb of laying a charge, so it sits beside crime, criminal, and accuse words.
note.cn: incriminate 是「把罪名按到人身上」的动词，与 crime、criminal 以及表示控告的词为邻。

entries.definition: a person who has broken the law, or relating to crime
entries.definitionCN: 罪犯；刑事的（同源形容词与名词）

entries.definition: the scientific study of crime
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪学（同源词）

entries.definition: making a person seem guilty
entries.definitionCN: 使人有罪的（动词的现在分词，已单独作形容词用）

entries.definition: to say that someone has done something wrong
entries.definitionCN: 指控；控告（多指公开说出某人做错事）

entries.definition: to say that a person is responsible for something bad
entries.definitionCN: 责怪；归咎于（语气比 incriminate 轻）

entries.definition: to show that someone is guilty
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人有罪（与 incriminate 几乎同义的正式法律用词）

normalIntro.en: Incriminate is a Latin charge laid on a person: in- plus crimen, the accusation.
normalIntro.cn: incriminate 是把一项指控按到某人身上的动作：in- 加上 crimen（指控）。

normal.en: The root crimen is the same charge that lives in crime and criminal.
normal.cn: 词根 crimen 就是 crime 与 criminal 里那份「罪名」。

normal.en: The prefix in- throws the charge onto the object, so the person is put inside the blame.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 把指控投到宾语身上，于是人被放进了罪责之内。

normal.en: Incriminating evidence is the everyday phrase for proof that pushes a person toward guilt.
normal.cn: incriminating evidence 是日常里最常用的说法，指把人推向有罪的证据。

normal.en: The right against self-incrimination means the law will not force you to make your own charge.
normal.cn: 反对自证其罪的权利，意思是法律不会强迫你自己制造对自己的指控。

normal.en: Compare accuse: accuse names the act of saying, incriminate names the act of making a person seem guilty.
normal.cn: 对比 accuse：accuse 重在「说出」，incriminate 重在「使人显得有罪」。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope dropping onto the empty chair in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的信封落在法庭里空着的那把椅子上。

abstract.en: See a fingerprint rising off glass and pointing straight at one face.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚指纹从玻璃上浮起来，直直指向一张脸。

abstract.en: Think of a spotlight swinging around a crowded room until it stops on you.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯扫过满屋的人，最后停在你自己身上。

examples.en: The police searched the flat for anything that might incriminate the suspect.
examples.cn: 警方搜查公寓，寻找任何可能证明嫌疑人有罪的东西。

examples.en: Her diary contained several incriminating entries.
examples.cn: 她的日记里有几处内容可能成为对自己不利的证据。

examples.en: Lawyers argued that the question forced the client to incriminate himself.
examples.cn: 律师辩称，那个提问迫使当事人自证其罪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬扣罪名」——把罪名「硬扣」到某个人头上，就是 incriminate；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语名词 crimen/ criminis（指控、罪名；来源不确定，一般认为源自动词 cernere「分辨、裁决」的派生名词 cernimen）+ 前缀 in-（进入、向内）→ incriminare（控告）→ 经晚期拉丁语与法语进入英语动词 incriminate，核心义「把罪名按到某人身上」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses move from the core charge of guilt to involving others, to evidence that proves guilt, to words against oneself, and finally to false charges and suspicious things.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从一个「罪名」出发：先让某人显得有罪，再把他人卷进来，再让证据去证明，进而说对自己不利的话，最后扩展到诬陷和可疑之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a charge laid on a person like a heavy object dropping onto their shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：一项罪名像重物一样落到某人肩上。

branches.en: THE PERSON UNDER THE CHARGE: either the accused alone or the accused plus someone dragged in.
branches.cn: 被指控的人：既可以是被告本人，也可以再拖上另一个人。

branches.en: THE TOOL BECOMES THE ACCUSER: evidence or a written note points at the person.
branches.cn: 工具变成控告者：证据或字条反过来指向那个人。

branches.en: THE SPEAKER TURNS INWARD: the words of the accused become the charge.
branches.cn: 说话人转向自身：被告自己说出的话成了指控。

branches.en: THE FALSE VERSION: the charge may be planted, so the verb can mean to frame.
branches.cn: 虚假版本：指控可能被栽种，于是词义可以变成「诬陷」。

branches.en: FROM LEGAL TO EVERYDAY: any suspicious detail can incriminate a scene.
branches.cn: 从法律走向日常：任何可疑细节都能让一个场景显得不利。

intro.en: Incriminate is built from the Latin prefix in- and the noun stem crimin-, with English suffixes making the rest of the family.
intro.cn: incriminate 由拉丁语前缀 in- 与名词词干 crimin- 构成，英语再加后缀形成整个词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is the noun crimen and the verb incriminare; English keeps both the noun family and the verbal family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是名词 crimen 与动词 incriminare，英语同时保留了名词族与动词族。

items.example: In- places the charge onto the object.
items.exampleCN: in- 把指控加在宾语身上。

items.example: The stem crimin- carries the idea of accusation.
items.exampleCN: 词干 crimin- 携带「指控」的意思。

items.example: Incriminare is the direct Latin source verb.
items.exampleCN: incriminare 是直接的拉丁语源动词。

items.example: Crimen supplies both crime and criminal.
items.exampleCN: crimen 提供了 crime 与 criminal 的源头。

items.example: The suffix -ate turns the noun stem into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把名词词干变成动词。

items.example: Incriminate keeps the legal sense in English.
items.exampleCN: incriminate 在英语中保留了法律含义。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词与形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms incriminating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 incriminating。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms incrimination.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 incrimination。

items.meaning: the act of making someone seem guilty
items.example: Incrimination names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: incrimination 指这个动作本身。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms incriminatory.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 构成 incriminatory。

definition_zh: 招致；惹起（不快）；蒙受；背负（费用、债务）
definition_en: to experience something unpleasant as a result of your own actions
core_image: 一个人沿路往前走，脚后跟不断带起尘土，账单与麻烦跟着落进他的背包
scene: 施工队日夜赶工，结果招来了邻里的强烈不满。The crew worked through the night and incurred the anger of the neighbours.
sceneCN: 这里 incur 是「招致、惹起」（第 1 个义项：因自身行为惹来不愉快的事），赶工正是把不满招到手的原因；句意：施工队通宵作业，招来了邻居们的怒气。

pos.zh: 招致；惹起；蒙受；承担（费用、债务）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「招致；发生（费用、负债）」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可能招致的」

senses.title: To bring something unpleasant on yourself
senses.definition: to cause something unpleasant such as anger or criticism to be directed at you by your own actions
senses.definitionCN: 因自己的行为而使不快之事（如愤怒、批评）落到自己头上
senses.example: Any delay would incur the manager s displeasure.
senses.exampleCN: 任何延误都会使经理不快。
senses.why: The Latin prefix in- means against or upon, and currere means to run, so the unpleasant thing runs against you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 意为「朝、对着」，currere 意为「跑」，于是不愉快的事正是朝你跑来、落到你身上。

senses.title: To have to pay a cost
senses.definition: to become responsible for paying a cost as a result of an action or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 因某项行动或安排而需要支付一笔费用
senses.example: The repair work will incur extra costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修将产生额外费用。
senses.why: Once the verb means taking on what follows an action, money is the most concrete thing to take on.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「承担行为带来的后果」，钱便是最具体的那种后果，于是有了「产生、承担费用」。

senses.title: To take on a debt or other burden
senses.definition: to take on a debt, an obligation, or another lasting burden
senses.definitionCN: 背上债务、义务或其他持久的负担
senses.example: The family incurred heavy debts during the year.
senses.exampleCN: 这一年里一家人背上了沉重的债务。
senses.why: A debt runs on beyond the moment of paying, so it is something carried forward.
senses.whyCN: 债务在付款的那一刻之后还在延续，因此它成为可以被「背负」着的长久负担。

senses.title: To suffer a loss or a penalty
senses.definition: to suffer a financial loss, a fine, or another punishment
senses.definitionCN: 遭受经济损失、罚款或其他惩罚
senses.example: Late payment incurs a penalty of two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 逾期付款会招致百分之二的罚款。
senses.why: Since the object is whatever follows from an act, a loss or a fine fits the same slot.
senses.whyCN: 既然宾语就是行为带来的后果，那么损失与罚款也落在同一个宾语位置上。

senses.title: To expose yourself to a risk
senses.definition: to put yourself in a position where a risk or a danger becomes possible
senses.definitionCN: 使自己处在可能遭遇风险或危险的位置上
senses.example: Drivers who ignore the rules incur the risk of accident.
senses.exampleCN: 无视规则的司机会让自己面临事故风险。
senses.why: The running image shows the consequence approaching from ahead, which is exactly the shape of a risk.
senses.whyCN: 「跑向」的画面里，后果是从前方迎面而来的，这恰好就是风险的运动方向。

senses.title: To become liable to a legal consequence
senses.definition: to become legally subject to a duty, a charge, or a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上负有某项义务、责任或处罚
senses.example: Anyone who breaks the contract will incur liability for damages.
senses.exampleCN: 任何违反合同的人都将承担损害赔偿责任。
senses.why: Legal writing took the everyday verb and fixed it to duties and liabilities that attach to a person.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书把这个日常动词固定用来指附着在人身上的义务与责任，于是常有「依法招致」的说法。

intro.en: Incur comes from the Latin verb incurrere, to run into or run upon, made of in- and currere.
intro.cn: incur 来自拉丁语动词 incurrere（跑进去、撞上），由 in- 与 currere 合成。

items.en: Currere means to run, the root of many running words.
items.cn: currere 意为「跑」，是许多与奔跑有关词语的共同词根。

items.en: Incurrere adds in- and means to run into or come upon.
items.cn: incurrere 加上 in- 后，意为「跑入、遭遇」。

items.en: The verb already covers running into trouble or blame.
items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语里，这个动词已可指「遭遇麻烦或指责」。

items.en: The verb enters English and keeps the idea of bringing something upon oneself.
items.cn: 十五世纪前后，这个词进入英语，保留了「把某事招到自己身上」的含义。

items.en: The sense of suffering a loss or a legal duty becomes standard.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，「蒙受损失」与「负法定义务」的用法成为标准。

items.en: Finance and law make incur a fixed partner of cost, debt, and liability.
items.cn: 现代英语中，金融与法律语境让 incur 与费用、债务、责任成为固定搭配。

note.en: Incur is a running verb of consequence, so it sits beside its Latin root and beside the verbs of causing and bearing.
note.cn: incur 是「后果跑向自己」的动词，与它的拉丁词根以及表示招致、承担的动词为邻。

entries.definition: the flow of water or electricity, or happening now
entries.definitionCN: 水流；电流；当前的（同源，来自「跑」的词根）

entries.definition: to happen or come to mind
entries.definitionCN: 发生；浮现（同源，字面为「跑到某处」）

entries.definition: to happen again
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生（同源，字面为「再跑回来」）

entries.definition: to experience something bad
entries.definitionCN: 遭受（强调承受痛苦，不强调自招）

entries.definition: to carry a cost or a burden
entries.definitionCN: 承担；承受（侧重背负的负担）

entries.definition: to cause something bad to begin
entries.definitionCN: 引起；招来（短语动词，与 incur 第一义项相近）

normalIntro.en: Incur is the running verb currere with in- attached: trouble runs into you.
normalIntro.cn: incur 是「跑」的动词 currere 加上 in-：麻烦朝你跑过来。

normal.en: The root currere gives current, occur, and recur, all about flowing or running.
normal.cn: 词根 currere 生成 current、occur、recur，都与流动、奔跑有关。

normal.en: In- means toward or upon, so incur is something running onto the subject.
normal.cn: in- 表示「朝向、压上」，所以 incur 是某种东西朝主语跑过来。

normal.en: The double r in incurred and incurring follows the rule for stressed final syllables.
normal.cn: incurred 与 incurring 里双写 r，遵循重读末尾辅音双写的规则。

normal.en: In business writing, costs and debts are the strongest partners of incur.
normal.cn: 在商务写作里，费用与债务是 incur 最固定的搭档。

normal.en: Compare occur: occur is something happening to the world, incur is something happening to you.
normal.cn: 对比 occur：occur 是世界在发生，incur 是事情落到你自己身上。

abstract.en: Picture a runner on a road and a storm rolling toward them from ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象一个奔跑的人，同时一团风暴正从同一个方向朝他滚来。

abstract.en: See an invoice thrown like a frisbee and landing in your bag.
abstract.cn: 想象一张账单像飞盘一样被扔出，落进你的背包。

abstract.en: Imagine every careless step leaving a heavier stone in your pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象每走错一步，口袋里就多了一块更重的石头。

examples.en: Companies that ignore safety rules may incur heavy fines.
examples.cn: 无视安全规定的公司可能会招致巨额罚款。

examples.en: She incurred a large debt to finish her studies.
examples.cn: 为了完成学业，她背上了一大笔债务。

examples.en: The team incurred the criticism of local residents.
examples.cn: 这个团队招来了当地居民的批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in 卡」——麻烦「卡」进了自己身上，就是 incur；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入、朝） + currere（跑）→ incurrere（跑入、撞上、遭遇）→ 英语 incur，核心义「有后果朝你跑来、落到你身上」。
