sensesIntro.en: Six senses start from unpleasant things brought on by oneself, then move to money, debts, losses and penalties, to risk, and finally to legal liability.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从「自己招来的不快」出发，依次走向费用、债务、损失与罚款，再到风险，最后到法律责任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walking forward while trouble rolls onto them from the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人往前走，麻烦却从正面滚到他身上。

branches.en: THE EMOTIONAL OUTCOME: anger or criticism arrives from someone ahead.
branches.cn: 情绪后果：愤怒或批评从前方的人那里到来。

branches.en: THE MONEY OUTCOME: costs arrive at once, debts stay and grow.
branches.cn: 金钱后果：费用是一次性到来的，债务则留下来并不断累积。

branches.en: THE PUNISHING OUTCOME: a loss or a fine lands on the subject.
branches.cn: 惩罚后果：损失或罚款落在主语头上。

branches.en: THE POSSIBLE OUTCOME: nothing has arrived yet, only a risk is opened.
branches.cn: 可能的后果：什么都还没到来，只打开了一扇风险之门。

branches.en: THE LEGAL OUTCOME: a burden is fixed by contract or law, as with liability.
branches.cn: 法律后果：负担由合同或法律固定下来，例如法律责任。

intro.en: Incur is a Latin verb made of the prefix in- and the verb currere; English adds only a few inflected forms and rare derived nouns.
intro.cn: incur 是由前缀 in- 与动词 currere 组成的拉丁动词，英语几乎只增加屈折形式与少量稀有派生名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pair is currere, to run, and incurrere, to run into; their family also gives English occur, recur, and current.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的一对词是 currere（跑）与 incurrere（跑入），它们还生成英语的 occur、recur、current。

items.example: In- gives the direction of running into.
items.exampleCN: in- 给出「跑进去」的方向。

items.example: The stem curr- carries the motion of running.
items.exampleCN: 词干 curr- 携带奔跑的动作。

items.example: Currere is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: currere 是这一词族的基础动词。

items.example: Incurrere is the direct source of incur.
items.exampleCN: incurrere 是 incur 的直接来源。

items.example: Occur keeps the running root with the prefix ob-.
items.exampleCN: occur 用前缀 ob- 保留了「跑」的词根。

items.meaning: to run back, to happen again
items.example: Recur adds the prefix re- to the same root.
items.exampleCN: recur 在同一词根前加了前缀 re-。

items.example: Current shows the flowing sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: current 体现了词根「流动」的一面。

items.example: Incurred doubles the final r before the suffix.
items.exampleCN: incurred 在词尾前双写 r。

items.example: Incurring also doubles the final r.
items.exampleCN: incurring 同样双写词尾 r。

items.example: The suffix -ence forms incurrence.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ence 构成 incurrence。

definition_zh: 犹豫不决；优柔寡断；踌躇
definition_en: the state of being unable to decide what to do
core_image: 一只手悬在两张门之间，既不推开这一扇，也不推开那一扇
scene: 菜单摊开了很久，客人在两道菜之间始终拿不定主意。After a long look at the menu, the guest sat in indecision.
sceneCN: 这里 indecision 是「犹豫不决」（第 1 个义项：迟迟拿不定主意），客人面对菜单正是这种状态；句意：看了很久菜单后，客人陷入了犹豫。

pos.zh: 犹豫不决；优柔寡断；踌躇

derivatives.zh: 由词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「犹豫不决的；优柔寡断的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「犹豫不决地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「优柔寡断」

senses.title: The state of not being able to choose
senses.definition: the condition of being unable to make a choice
senses.definitionCN: 无法做出选择的状态
senses.example: After a long pause of indecision, she ordered soup.
senses.exampleCN: 犹豫了好一阵之后，她点了汤。
senses.why: The Latin prefix in- means not, and decidere means to cut off, so indecision is the state in which no option has been cut off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 表示「不」，decidere 意为「切下、裁断」；犹豫就是没有任何一个选项被「切掉」的状态。

senses.title: A habit of mind that is slow to act
senses.definition: a lasting habit or manner of being slow to make decisions
senses.definitionCN: 长期难以做出决定的性格或做事风格
senses.example: His indecision cost the company a good chance.
senses.exampleCN: 他的优柔寡断让公司错失了一个好机会。
senses.why: The state sense is counted, so a habit that repeats becomes a quality of the person.
senses.whyCN: 「状态」义项可以被反复计数，当其成为习惯时，就扩展为对一个人性格的评价。

senses.title: A pause in the middle of an act
senses.definition: a short hesitation or pause in the middle of speaking or acting
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或行动中途出现的短暂停顿和迟疑
senses.example: There was indecision in his voice before he answered.
senses.exampleCN: 回答之前，他的声音里带着迟疑。
senses.why: A longer frozen state also appears in miniature as a handful of seconds inside one sentence.
senses.whyCN: 长久的状态也可以以缩影的形式出现，也就是一句话中间那短短几秒的停顿。

senses.title: A vote that reaches no result
senses.definition: a failure of a group or a meeting to reach a clear decision
senses.definitionCN: 团体或会议没能形成明确决定的情形
senses.example: The committee ended its meeting in indecision.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的会议以议而未决收场。
senses.why: The inability to cut off options can belong to an assembled body as easily as to one person.
senses.whyCN: 「无法切掉选项」的主体既可以是个人，也可以是一群聚在一起表决的人。

senses.title: Uncertainty shown on a face or in a voice
senses.definition: a visible or audible sign of being unsure of what to say or do
senses.definitionCN: 在神情或语气上显露出的不确定迹象
senses.example: The slight indecision in her smile made us wait.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑容里那点犹豫，让我们决定再等等。
senses.why: The inner state becomes visible, so observers can read indecision off a face.
senses.whyCN: 内在状态外显之后，旁人便可以从脸上读出这份犹豫。

intro.en: Indecision combines the negative prefix in- with decision, which came through French from the Latin verb decidere.
intro.cn: indecision 由否定前缀 in- 与 decision 合成，后者经法语来自拉丁语动词 decidere。

items.en: Decidere is made of de- and caedere, to cut, and means to cut off.
items.cn: decidere 由 de- 与 caedere（切）构成，本义为「切下」。

items.en: The verb widens from cutting off to settling or deciding a matter.
items.cn: 这个动词从「切下」扩展为「裁定、决定」。

items.en: The noun based on the verb reaches French early on.
items.cn: 由该动词构成的名词很早就进入法语。

items.en: Decision is borrowed with the sense of a settled judgement.
items.cn: 十六世纪，decision 以「已定下的判断」之义被借入英语。

items.en: The negative noun indecision appears with the prefix in-.
items.cn: 十七世纪，带前缀 in- 的否定名词 indecision 出现。

items.en: The word settles into everyday description of people and meetings.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词固定用于描述个人与会议中的迟疑。

note.en: Indecision is the negative noun of deciding, so it sits beside all the words that name a choice.
note.cn: indecision 是「决定」的否定名词，与所有表示选择的词为邻。

entries.definition: able to make choices quickly and firmly
entries.definitionCN: 果断的（与 indecision 正相对）

entries.definition: slow and unsure in making choices
entries.definitionCN: 优柔寡断的（同一词根的形容词）

entries.definition: a choice that has been made
entries.definitionCN: 决定（加否定前缀后形成 indecision）

entries.definition: a pause before acting because of doubt
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫；迟疑（侧重动作前的片刻停顿）

entries.definition: a feeling of not being sure
entries.definitionCN: 怀疑；不确定（侧重对答案本身没把握）

entries.definition: the state of not knowing what will happen
entries.definitionCN: 不确定性（可指对未来的把握不足）

normalIntro.en: Indecision is decision with the negative prefix in- in front: no line has been cut.
normalIntro.cn: indecision 就是 decision 前面加了否定前缀 in-：一条线也没被切下来。

normal.en: The verb decidere broke down a knot by cutting it, and decision inherited that cutting image.
normal.cn: 动词 decidere 用「切」的方式解开纠结，decision 继承了这份切开的意象。

normal.en: The prefix in- negates, so indecision is decision that has not happened yet.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 表示否定，所以 indecision 是尚未发生的决定。

normal.en: A state of indecision is a countable phrase, which is why the plural indecisions can appear.
normal.cn: 「a state of indecision」是一种可数的说法，所以复数 indecisions 也能出现。

normal.en: The adjective is indecisive, and the base adjective decisive simply drops the negative prefix.
normal.cn: 对应的形容词是 indecisive，而正面形式 decisive 本身不含否定前缀。

normal.en: Compare hesitation: hesitation is a short pause, indecision is the wider condition behind it.
normal.cn: 对比 hesitation：hesitation 是短暂停顿，indecision 是它背后更广的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scissors held half open above a knot, never closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一把剪刀悬在一个结的上方，半开不合。

abstract.en: See two paths crossing and a shadow standing on the point where they meet.
abstract.cn: 想象两条小路交叉，一个人影正停在他们相交的那一点。

abstract.en: Imagine a cursor blinking on a form that says choose one.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上光标在待选的空白处一下一下闪烁。

examples.en: Her indecision about the job lasted for weeks.
examples.cn: 她为这份工作犹豫了好几个星期。

examples.en: He stood at the door in indecision, listening to the voices inside.
examples.cn: 他站在门口犹豫着，听着里面的说话声。

examples.en: The board was criticized for its indecision over the new plan.
examples.cn: 董事会因对这项新计划迟迟不决而受到批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬底细」——关键「底细」不清楚，就一直犹豫不定，这就是 indecision；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ decidere（de- 离开 + caedere 切，义为「切下、裁断；来源不确定，一般认为与 caedere 同源」）→ 晚期拉丁语 decidere（决定）→ 法语 → 英语 decision，再加否定前缀 in- 得 indecision，核心义「迟迟不肯切下某个选项」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses start from a frozen state of choosing, then widen to a lasting habit, a short pause, a meeting without result, and a look on a face.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从「选不下去的冻结状态」出发，扩展为持久的性格、短暂的停顿、会议上的议而未决，以及写在脸上的迟疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand hanging between two doors, touching neither.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手悬在两道门之间，哪一扇也没推开。

branches.en: THE FROZEN STATE: no choice has been cut off, so the mind simply waits.
branches.cn: 冻结状态：没有一个选项被切掉，心于是只能干等。

branches.en: THE HABIT: the same freeze repeated over time turns into a character judgement.
branches.cn: 习惯：同一种冻结反复出现，就变成对人的性格评价。

branches.en: THE SMALL VERSION: a pause inside speech or action, or a flicker on a face.
branches.cn: 微型版本：一句话里的一次停顿，或脸上一闪而过的迟疑。

branches.en: THE SHARED VERSION: when a whole group fails to cut, the noun moves from people to meetings.
branches.cn: 集体版本：当一群人一同切不下去时，这个词就从个人移到会议上。

branches.en: BOTH ENDS: from one person at a menu to a committee with no result, it is the same missing cut.
branches.cn: 两端：从点菜的一个人到无果的委员会，缺的都是同一刀。

intro.en: Indecision is the negative prefix in- plus decision, whose stems are Latin de-, -cid-, and the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: indecision 由否定前缀 in- 与 decision 组成，后者的构词成分是拉丁语 de-、词根 -cid- 与名词后缀 -ion。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verbs caedere and decidere supply the cutting image, while decisio is the noun behind decision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 caedere 与 decidere 提供「切」的意象，名词 decisio 则是 decision 的来源。

items.example: In- makes the noun negative.
items.exampleCN: in- 使这个名词带有否定意味。

items.example: The stem -cid- carries the cutting image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -cid- 携带「切」的意象。

items.example: Caedere is the base verb behind the stem.
items.exampleCN: caedere 是词根背后的基础动词。

items.example: De- adds the sense of cutting off.
items.exampleCN: de- 增添了「切下」的方向感。

items.example: Decidere grows from cutting to settling a matter.
items.exampleCN: decidere 从「切」发展为「裁定」。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms decision.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 decision。

items.meaning: a choice that has been made
items.example: Decision is the base noun of indecision.
items.exampleCN: decision 是 indecision 的基础名词。

items.example: Indecision names the missing choice.
items.exampleCN: indecision 指那一项缺失的选择。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms indecisive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 indecisive。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms indecisiveness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 indecisiveness。

definition_zh: 不知疲倦的；不屈不挠的；持之以恒的；孜孜不倦的
definition_en: never becoming tired or losing energy in what one undertakes, and persisting through difficulty
core_image: 一个人走了很远的路，鞋面磨破，脚步却依旧平稳不停
scene: 老人沿着河堤来回巡查了整整一夜，直到天亮也不肯坐下歇脚。The indefatigable watchman walked the bank until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 indefatigable 是「不知疲倦的；孜孜不倦的」（第 1 个义项：做事从不显出疲劳）；句意为这位不知疲倦的守夜人沿河堤走到了天亮。图中可辨识物件：磨破的布鞋、堤岸、提灯。

pos.zh: 不知疲倦的；不屈不挠的；孜孜不倦的

collocations.zh: 不屈不挠地反对不公的人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不知疲倦地；坚持不懈地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「不知疲倦；坚韧不拔」
同根的独立词，义为「疲劳；使疲劳」，是 indis 与 fatigabilis 所否定的那个词根
去掉否定前缀后的罕见形式，义为「会疲劳的」，多出现在刻意对照的写作里

senses.title: Never showing signs of tiredness
senses.definition: able to go on working for a very long time without looking tired
senses.definitionCN: 能长时间工作而不显疲态
senses.example: Her indefatigable cheerfulness kept the team going.
senses.exampleCN: 她那不知疲倦的乐观让整个团队撑了下来。
senses.why: The Latin in- denies fatigabilis, that which can be tired out, so the word names a person whom weariness cannot touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 否定了 fatigabilis（会被累垮的），所以这个词形容的是一种疲惫无法触及的人。

senses.title: Persisting despite resistance
senses.titleCN: 不屈不挠的；顽强坚持的
senses.definition: continuing to work for something although people or conditions resist it
senses.definitionCN: 尽管遭到人或情势的阻力，仍继续为某个目标努力
senses.example: An indefatigable minority pushed for the law for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 一个不屈不挠的少数群体为这项法律奔走了三十年。
senses.why: The same image of an unhurried walker turns moral: persistence that simply does not stop is a kind of courage.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「步不停歇」的画面转向道德层面：怎么都不肯停下来的坚持，本身就是一种勇气。

senses.title: Untiring in a pursuit or search
senses.titleCN: 孜孜不倦的；锲而不舍的
senses.definition: never slackening in a study, a search, or a hunt
senses.definitionCN: 在研究、寻找或追查中从不见松懈
senses.example: The detective was indefatigable in chasing every loose thread.
senses.exampleCN: 这位侦探追查每一条线索时都锲而不舍。
senses.why: Casual visitors to the word notice that it often sits beside mental work: an untiring intelligence, an untiring enquiry.
senses.whyCN: 细看会发现这个词常与脑力劳动为伴，例如不知疲倦的头脑、不知疲倦的追问，于是从体力层面延伸到求知层面。

senses.title: Applied to things and habits
senses.titleCN: 形容事物：出个不停的；周而复始的
senses.definition: of an activity or object, going on so steadily that it seems never to stop
senses.definitionCN: 指活动或事物持续得如此稳定，几乎像永不停歇
senses.example: The garden thrived on her indefatigable watering each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园靠她每天早晨不知疲倦的浇灌而繁茂。
senses.why: When the describing words for people move to their actions, the picture of a tireless body becomes a habit that repeats by itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容人的词一旦转去修饰其行为，那个「不倦的身体」就变成会自动重复的习惯，事物因此带上不知停顿的性质。

intro.en: Indefatigable is a Renaissance borrowing from French and Latin: the negative in- laid over fatigabilis, which comes from fatigare, to tire.
intro.cn: indefatigable 是文艺复兴时期从法语与拉丁语引入的借词：否定前缀 in- 加在 fatigabilis 之上，而 fatigabilis 出自 fatigare（使疲劳）。

items.en: Fatigare meant to tire or weary, but its own source is uncertain: one guess links it to a word for gap or opening, another to something pressed down. No result here depends on that guess.
items.cn: fatigare 意为使疲劳，但它自身的来源不确定：一种猜测把它连到表示「缝隙、开口」的词，另一种连到「被压下去」的含义；下面的结论都不依赖这个猜测。

items.en: The adjective fatigabilis described anything able to be tired out, with the -bilis ending for what can be done.
items.cn: 形容词 fatigabilis 描述任何会被累垮的东西，词尾 -bilis 表示「能被……的」。

items.en: Adding the negative prefix in- produced indefatigabilis, not to be tired out.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀 in- 之后得到 indefatigabilis，义为「不能被累垮的」。

items.en: French indefatigable carried the same negative build into a newer spelling.
items.cn: 法语 indefatigable 沿用同样的否定结构，只是拼写更新。

items.en: English adopted the word for writers, workers, and reformers who simply keep going.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用来形容始终不肯停下的写作者、工作者与改革者。

items.en: Today the word is mostly formal praise, common in reports and obituaries.
items.cn: 今天这个词多用于正式的赞语，常见于报道与讣闻。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same tire-root; the second collects adjectives for persistence and for the opposite quality.
note.cn: 第一组收「疲劳」词根上的同族词；第二组收表示坚持的近义词以及反义对照词。

entries.definition: great tiredness, or to make someone very tired
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「极度疲劳；使疲劳」，正是本词否定掉的那个概念

entries.definition: making you feel very tired
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「令人疲惫的」，本词正是它的反面

entries.definition: a rarer spelling of the same word, now dated
entries.definitionCN: 同词的少见拼写，现已过时；与本词拼写相近但少一个 de 音节

entries.definition: working hard for a long time without getting tired
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「不知疲倦的」；比本词口语，可形容人与活动

entries.definition: never becoming weaker or less enthusiastic
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「不松懈的」，侧重热情与劲头不减

entries.definition: continuing to do something in spite of difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「坚持不懈的」，更中性，也常带固执的意味

normalIntro.en: Split the word honestly: in plus de plus fatigable, meaning not able to be tired out.
normalIntro.cn: 拆开看就好记：in 加 de 加 fatigable，合起来就是「不会被累垮的」。

normal.en: Fatigable means able to be worn out, so indefatigable means the opposite of being worn out.
normal.cn: fatigable 意为「会被累垮的」，所以 indefatigable 就是不会被累垮。

normal.en: The related noun fatigue is the tiredness that the word denies.
normal.cn: 同根名词 fatigue 就是这个词所否定的「疲劳」。

normal.en: The adverb indefatigably keeps the middle a of fatiga intact.
normal.cn: 副词 indefatigably 保留了中间 fatig- 的那段字母，拼写别漏掉 a。

normal.en: In IELTS writing it is a formal word for praise, so use it sparingly for people, not for machines.
normal.cn: 它是正式的赞美词，雅思写作中宜少量使用，多形容人而不形容机器。

normal.en: Compare tireless: tireless is plainer and more common; indefatigable is formal and literary.
normal.cn: 对比 tireless：tireless 更平淡常用，indefatigable 正式且带文学色彩。

abstract.en: Imagine a runner four hours in who still counts each breath evenly.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑了四小时的跑者，呼吸依旧一口一口数得均匀。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil that never runs out of lead while the writer keeps talking to the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一支永远写不完的铅笔，而写字的人一直对着纸页说话。

abstract.en: Think of a candle beside an open window that keeps burning though the wind never stops.
abstract.cn: 想象窗边一支蜡烛，风一直吹，火苗却一直不灭。

examples.en: The indefatigable nurse stayed on the ward through two night shifts.
examples.cn: 那位不知疲倦的护士连值了两个夜班，一直守在病房里。

examples.en: His indefatigable research habits earned him three major prizes.
examples.cn: 他孜孜不倦的研究习惯为他赢得了三个大奖。

examples.en: Critics called the book an indefatigable record of a forgotten town.
examples.cn: 评论家称这本书是对一座被遗忘小镇不知疲倦的记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因得伐体该勃」——因为得到了伐木的力气，身体再也不该疲惫；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fatigare「使疲劳」→ fatigabilis「会被累垮的」→ 加否定前缀 in- 得 indefatigabilis「不会被累垮的」→ 经法语 indefatigable → 英语 indefatigable；核心义「疲惫奈何不了他」。fatigare 自身的最早来源不确定，一词源假说把它连到表示「缝隙」的词，此处不据此展开。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with the plain picture of a worker who never tires, then widens to stubborn persistence, to untiring study, and finally to actions and things that seem never to stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先是一幅「干活从不喊累」的直白画面，随后扩展到倔强的坚持、不知倦的求索，最后用在活动与事物身上，形容仿佛永不停歇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker whose shoes are worn through, still keeping an even pace.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个鞋子都磨破了的行人，脚步依旧平平稳稳。

branches.en: A person who shows no sign of tiredness is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 不显出疲态的人是最直接的义项。

branches.en: Refusing to give in against resistance is the moral extension.
branches.cn: 顶着阻力不放手的用法是道德层面的延伸。

branches.en: Untiring study and search is the mental sense.
branches.cn: 用于研究与追查是从脑力角度使用这个义项。

branches.en: When it describes actions or objects, the habit itself seems never to pause.
branches.cn: 用来形容动作或物件时，强调习惯性的周而复始。

branches.en: All three senses share one picture: weariness is denied, so the effort continues.
branches.cn: 这三个义项共享一幅画面：否定疲惫，所以努力继续。

intro.en: The word is built from a negative prefix and a Latin can-be-tired adjective, with the plain English word fatigue as its visible anchor.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个否定前缀和一个表示「会被累垮」的拉丁语形容词搭成，最直观的锚点是英语里常见的 fatigue。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the plan: in- for not, fatigabilis for able to be tired, and -lis for ability.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把结构说得很清楚：in- 表示「不」，fatigabilis 表示「会被累垮」，词尾 -lis 表示「能够」。

items.example: The prefix turns being tired into not being tired.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「疲劳」翻成「不疲劳」。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea of weariness itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「疲惫」本身的概念。

items.example: This adjective is the part directly denied by in-.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词正是 in- 所直接否定的部分。

items.example: The suffix marks capacity in words such as readable and visible.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀在读作「可读的」与「可见的」等词里标出能力。

items.meaning: not able to be tired out
items.example: This late Latin form is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁语形式是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The English adjective keeps the whole Latin build.
items.exampleCN: 英语形容词完整保留了拉丁语的结构。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质或能力的词尾
items.example: The ending -able turns the Latin concept into this English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 把这个拉丁概念变成英语形容词。

items.example: Adding -ly produces the adverb used for manner.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ly 得到修饰方式或程度的副词。

items.example: Adding -ity yields indefatigability, the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ity 得到 indefatigability，指这种品质本身。

items.example: Fatigue is the everyday word hidden inside the longer form.
items.exampleCN: fatigue 就藏在这个长词的里面，是最日常的那个词。

definition_zh: 使缩进；首行缩进；在……上压出凹痕；锯齿状切口；订货单
definition_en: to start a line of writing further from the margin, to press a notch into a surface, or a notched cut itself
core_image: 纸边被咬出一排小齿，正文从齿痕之后才起笔
scene: 编辑用红笔在稿纸边轻轻按出一个缺口，又从缺口之后写下第一句。The editor asked her to indent the first line of every paragraph.
sceneCN: 这里 indent 是「使缩进；首行缩进」（第 1 个义项：让一行字离开页边）；句意为编辑要她把每个段落的第一行都缩进。图中可辨识物件：红笔、稿纸、页边缺口。

pos.zh: 使缩进；在……上打缺口或压凹痕
缩格书写；形成锯齿状缺口
缩进；凹陷；锯齿状切口；订单

collocations.phrase: indent the edge of the page

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「缩进；凹陷；齿状缺口」
由本词加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「缩进的；边缘呈齿状的」
由本词加 -ure 构成，原指带齿状切口的合同，后指「契约；契约文书」
同族基础词，义为「凹痕；使凹陷」，本词正是它的加强形式

senses.title: To set a line in from the margin
senses.definition: to begin a line of writing farther from the edge of the page than the rest
senses.definitionCN: 使一行文字的起点比其他行更离开页边
senses.example: Indent every new paragraph by two spaces.
senses.exampleCN: 每个新段落都缩进两个空格。
senses.why: The core idea is a notched edge; a line pushed in from the margin looks as if it has been cut back into the page.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是边上的缺口；一行字从页边退进去，看上去就像被剪进了页面里。

senses.title: To cut teeth or notches along an edge
senses.definition: to cut a series of small sharp notches along the edge of something
senses.definitionCN: 沿某物的边缘打出一排小而尖的缺口
senses.example: Indent the card so the two halves fit like a puzzle.
senses.exampleCN: 把卡片边剪成锯齿状，两半就能像拼图一样咬合。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: a row of tooth-shaped cuts, which is the literal picture in the Latin root for tooth.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的实体义项：一排牙形切口，正是拉丁词根「牙」在字面上留下的那张画。

senses.title: To press a hollow into a surface
senses.definition: to make a dent or hollow impression in something by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用压力在某物表面压出凹陷
senses.example: A heavy crate had indented the floorboards.
senses.exampleCN: 一只重木箱在地板上压出了凹痕。
senses.why: A notch seen from the side is simply a hollow: the same shape, made by pressing or hammering instead of cutting.
senses.whyCN: 从侧面看，缺口就是一个洼陷：同一形状，只是改为压出或敲出，而不是剪出。

senses.title: A notched cut or hollow in an edge
senses.definition: a notch or hollow cut in an edge or a surface
senses.definitionCN: 切在边缘或表面上的一处缺口或凹陷
senses.example: The coastline shows a deep indent where the river enters.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸线在河流入海处内凹成一湾深缺口。
senses.why: Once the verb names the action, the noun names the leftover shape, and can even describe a bay bitten out of a coastline.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指动作，名词就指留下的形状，甚至能描述被大海「咬」出的海湾。

senses.title: A written order for goods
senses.definition: a written order, especially for supplies, historically a document cut in two matching halves
senses.definitionCN: 书面订货单，历史上指从中间剪成两半以便对合的文书
senses.example: The officer signed an indent for more medical supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 那位军官签了一张追加医疗用品的订单。
senses.why: Old orders were cut in a jagged line so the two halves matched; that toothed cut, not the goods, gave the sense its name.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的订单要从中间剪成锯齿状的两半以便对合；给这个义项取名的是那道齿痕，而不是货物本身。

intro.en: Indent goes back to Latin dens, dentis, a tooth, through a family of words for making a tooth-shaped cut; the English verb and noun both appeared in the late Middle Ages.
intro.cn: indent 上溯到拉丁语 dens, dentis（牙齿），经由一批表示「做出牙形切口」的词传来；英语的动词与名词都出现在中古英语后期。

items.en: Dens meant tooth, and its stem dent- is visible in dentist, dental and denture.
items.cn: dens 意为「牙齿」，其词干 dent- 在 dentist、dental 与 denture 里都看得见。

items.en: From that stem came verbs such as dentare, to furnish with teeth or to cut into points.
items.cn: 从这个词干派生出 dentare 一类动词，义为「装上齿」「切成尖齿」。

items.en: Old French endenter carried the sense of putting teeth into something, chiefly into paper or wood.
items.cn: 古法语 endenter 继承了「给某物（主要是纸或木头）装齿」的含义。

items.en: The in- that opens the word is usually explained as an intensive or locative prefix rather than the negative, a point on which accounts differ.
items.cn: 词首的 in- 一般解释为加强或方位前缀，而不是否定前缀；不同文献在这一点上说法不一。

items.en: English indent named cutting a document with a wavy edge, and soon the act of setting writing in from the margin.
items.cn: 英语 indent 先指把文书剪成波浪状边缘，很快又指让文字从页边缩进去。

items.en: Printing, then word processing, fixed the margin sense; railway and coastal geography kept the notch sense alive.
items.cn: 印刷业、继而是文字处理软件，把「页边」义固定下来；铁路与海岸地理的描述则让「缺口」义继续存活。

note.en: The first group follows the tooth-root and its English forms; the second gathers the margin words that indent is constantly compared with.
note.cn: 第一组沿「牙」词根及其英语词形展开；第二组收与本词经常混谈的页边类词语。

entries.definition: a set of spaces or a hollow where the edge is pushed in
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，义为「缩进；凹陷；齿状缺口」，是本词最常见名词

entries.definition: a legal contract, originally torn in a jagged line into matching halves
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「契约」，原指沿锯齿线撕成两半、可对合验证的文书

entries.definition: relating to teeth
entries.definitionCN: 同「牙」词根，义为「牙齿的、牙科的」，与 indent 共享同一个拉丁语词干 dent-

entries.definition: the blank space left around the edge of a page
entries.definitionCN: 近义（页边语场），义为「页边距；空白边缘」，indent 正是相对它而言

entries.definition: a distinct section of writing, often begun with a new indented line
entries.definitionCN: 相关语场，义为「段落」，常以首行缩进来开始的正是它

entries.definition: a V-shaped cut or indentation in an edge
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「V 形刻痕、缺口」；notch 只作名词或动词的实体义，indent 还专有排版义

normalIntro.en: The word is a cousin of dental: wherever a tooth-shaped cut appears, indent is nearby.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词与 dental 是同族：凡出现牙形切口的地方，附近多半就有 indent。

normal.en: Indent shares the dent- stem with dental and dentist, so think of a row of teeth along an edge.
normal.cn: indent 与 dental、dentist 共享 dent- 词干，所以先想边缘上的一排牙齿。

normal.en: The noun indentation is the most common form: a series of spaces at the start of a line.
normal.cn: 名词 indentation 是最常见的形态：一行开头的一串空格。

normal.en: Old indentures were cut in two along a jagged line, which is why indent once meant a contract.
normal.cn: 旧时的契约沿锯齿线剪成两半，这正是 indent 曾表示「契约」的原因。

normal.en: In essays indent each new paragraph, but never indent the first paragraph of an IELTS task.
normal.cn: 写文章时新段落要缩进，但雅思写作的正文第一段一般不缩进。

normal.en: Compare indent and indentation: the verb is the action, the longer noun is the resulting gap.
normal.cn: 对比 indent 与 indentation：动词指动作，较长的名词指留下的那段空白。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper whose left edge has been gently bitten, then the first words written just after the bite.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸的左边缘被轻轻咬过一口，第一行字正好从那道咬痕之后开始。

abstract.en: Imagine pressing a finger into soft clay and watching a shallow bowl appear.
abstract.cn: 想象把手指按进软泥里，眼看着一个小浅坑慢慢出现。

abstract.en: See a ticket torn into two halves with matching jagged edges, one kept by each party.
abstract.cn: 想一张票据被撕成两半，齿边正好对得上，双方各执一半。

examples.en: In most typed reports you indent the first line of every section.
examples.cn: 在大多数打印报告里，每个小节的第一行都要缩进。

examples.en: The old shipyard crane had indented the concrete over the years.
examples.cn: 多年来，港口的旧吊车在混凝土上压出了凹痕。

examples.en: An indent of four spaces marks a block of code in Python.
examples.cn: 在 Python 里，四个空格的一处缩进标出一个代码块。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印得特」——印出来的字特别往里去一点，就是首行缩进；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 dens, dentis「牙齿」（词干 dent-）→ dentare「切成齿状」→ 古法语 endenter「给……装齿、开齿口」→ 英语 indent；词首 in- 一般认为起加强或方位作用，而非否定，各家说法不完全一致。核心义「沿边咬出一排齿」。

sensesIntro.en: Indent starts from a physical row of tooth-shaped cuts, narrows into the printed margin, widens again to hollows and bays, and finally survives in the name of a torn order form.
sensesIntro.cn: indent 从一排实体的齿形切口出发，收窄为版面上的页边缩进，又扩散到凹陷与海湾，最后在一种被撕开的订单名字里留存下来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of small teeth cut into a paper edge, with writing starting after them.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸边被咬出一排小齿，文字从齿痕之后起笔。

branches.en: A line pushed in from the margin is the everyday printing sense.
branches.cn: 行首从页边退进去，是最日常的排版义项。

branches.en: Cutting real teeth along an edge keeps the oldest picture.
branches.cn: 在实物边缘切出真齿，保留了最古老的画面。

branches.en: Viewed sideways, the notch becomes a hollow pressed into a surface.
branches.cn: 换个角度看，缺口成了被压进表面的洼坑。

branches.en: The noun names the shape left behind, down to a bay in a coastline.
branches.cn: 名词义项命名留下的形状，小到一道凹口，大到海岸线上的海湾。

branches.en: Printed indents, torn documents and slotted orders all come from the same toothed cut.
branches.cn: 排版缩进、撕成两半的文书与开齿的订单都源自同一道齿形切口。

intro.en: Indent is held together by a tooth-root and a general prefix, with indentation, indented and indenture all radiating from it.
intro.cn: indent 由「牙」词根和一个通用前缀搭成，indentation、indented 与 indenture 都由它辐射出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin dens gives the stem dent-, meaning tooth, and -are or -atus endings turn that stem into verbs and adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dens 给出词干 dent-（牙齿），词尾 -are、-atus 再把它变成动词和形容词。

items.meaningCN: 向内、进入，或起加强语气的作用
items.example: The opening prefix here is usually read as intensive, not negative.
items.exampleCN: 这里的词首前缀一般读作加强，而不是否定。

items.example: The noun supplies the tooth that gives the notch its shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「牙」，正是它给了缺口那种形状。

items.example: The stem dent- lets dental, dentist and dentition all belong together.
items.exampleCN: 词干 dent- 让 dental、dentist 与 dentition 归在同一族。

items.example: The verb turns a tooth into an action of cutting teeth.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「牙」变成「切出牙形」的动作。

items.meaning: to furnish with teeth or a notched edge
items.meaningCN: 给某物装上齿或打出齿状边
items.example: Old French endenter handed the notched edge to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 endenter 把这个「齿状边」的概念交给英语。

items.meaning: to notch or set in from the margin
items.example: Both the English verb and noun keep the tooth cut.
items.exampleCN: 英语的动词与名词都保留着那道齿痕。

items.example: Adding -ation gives indentation, the act or result of indenting.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ation 得到 indentation，指缩进的动作或结果。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或工具的词尾
items.example: Adding -ure gives indenture, a contract made by a notched edge.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ure 得到 indenture，指靠齿状切口做成的契约。

items.example: The -ed ending makes a describing word of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 把动词变成描写性的形容词。

items.meaning: a shallow hollow, or to hollow something
items.example: Dent is the short plain word from the same root.
items.exampleCN: dent 是同一词根出来的简短日常词。

definition_zh: 起诉；正式控告；起诉书；对……的强烈谴责
definition_en: a formal legal accusation of a serious crime, the document that records it, or strong public criticism of something
core_image: 一张写满罪名的纸被当众念出，被念到名字的那个人低下头
scene: 大厅里人声低低作响，检察官把一页文件推过桌面，说要对那条旧街的市长提出正式控告。The grand jury returned an indictment against the mayor.
sceneCN: 这里 indictment 是「起诉；正式控告」（第 1 个义项：控告某人犯下重罪）；句意为大陪审团对市长作出了起诉。图中可辨识物件：一页文件、桌面、证人席座椅。

pos.zh: 起诉；正式控告；起诉书；对……的谴责

collocations.phrase: a damning indictment of the system

derivatives.zh: 由基础动词 indict 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「起诉；起诉书」
由 indict 加 -able 构成，义为「可被起诉的」
由 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新起诉；再次指控」

senses.title: A formal accusation of a serious crime
senses.definition: an official accusation charging someone with a serious crime, usually made after a grand jury examines the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 以正式名义指控某人犯下重罪，通常经大陪审团审查证据后作出
senses.example: Two businessmen face indictment for tax fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 两名商人因税务欺诈面临起诉。
senses.why: Latin in- here is not a negative but the prefix of pointing at a person, and dictare means to state; the word puts a charge into written words toward someone.
senses.whyCN: 这里的拉丁语前缀 in- 不是否定，而是「对着某人」的方向前缀，dictare 意为陈述；合起来就是就某人的案件写下指控。

senses.title: The document that records the charge
senses.definition: the written document in which the charges are set out
senses.definitionCN: 列明各项指控的书面文书
senses.example: The ninepage indictment listed twenty counts of bribery.
senses.exampleCN: 那份九页的起诉书列出了二十项贿赂指控。
senses.why: The act of stating a charge hardens into the paper itself; in legal practice the paper is what lawyers hand to reporters.
senses.whyCN: 陈述指控的动作凝结成那张纸；实务中律师递给记者、让人看见的正是这份文书。

senses.title: A strong public condemnation
senses.titleCN: （对制度、现象的）强烈谴责；控诉
senses.definition: a statement or situation showing that something is seriously wrong or unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事严重有误或不可接受的言论或局面
senses.example: The empty classrooms are an indictment of the funding cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡荡的教室是对削减经费的控诉。
senses.why: Once the word leaves the court it keeps the accusing tone: any fact that exposes a wrong becomes the charge, even without a judge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词离开法庭之后仍带着指控的口吻：凡是暴露了问题的事实，即使没有法官，也成了控诉本身。

senses.title: The state of being charged
senses.definition: the legal position of someone who has been charged until the case ends
senses.definitionCN: 从被起诉起到案件结束之前，被告所处的法律地位
senses.example: He resigned the day before the indictment was unsealed.
senses.exampleCN: 就在起诉书解封的前一天，他辞职了。
senses.why: In news English the noun often names the wound that follows the charge, so people speak of the shadow of indictment.
senses.whyCN: 在新闻英语里，这个名词常指指控之后留下的创口，于是人们会说处于起诉的阴影之中。

intro.en: Indictment belongs to the Latin verb dicere, to say, through indictus, the past participle of indicere, to declare or proclaim. Its spelling is medieval law French, its sound has drifted, and the silent c is the leftover of a word that was never pronounced that way.
intro.cn: indictment 根源在拉丁语动词 dicere（说），经由 indicere（宣布、宣告）的过去分词 indictus 而来。它的拼写出自中古时期的法制法语，读音却已经漂移，那个不发音的 c 正是从拉丁拼写传下来的痕迹。

items.en: Dicere meant to say or declare, and its participle dictus underlies dictate, dictionary and verdict.
items.cn: dicere 意为说、宣称，其分词 dictus 正是 dictate、dictionary 与 verdict 的共同来源。

items.en: Indicere was not the plain word for accuse; it meant to proclaim or give notice, sometimes to give notice of a charge.
items.cn: indicere 并不是「控告」的常用词，它指宣告、通知，偶尔用于「通知某项指控」。

items.en: In medieval legal Latin indictare narrowed to declaring a charge formally on the record.
items.cn: 在中世纪法律拉丁语中，indictare 收窄为「在案卷上正式宣告指控」。

items.en: French enditer or inditer carried the legal charge and also gave English indite, to write down.
items.cn: 法语 enditer 或 inditer 带来了这项法律指控，同时也给了英语 indite（书写）这条分支。

items.en: English indict meant to bring a charge, and the noun indictment followed it into the courts.
items.cn: 英语 indict 意为提出指控，名词 indictment 随之进入法庭。

items.en: Latin c was restored in the spelling centuries ago while the older sound stayed, and writers later widened the noun to general condemning.
items.cn: 拉丁语的 c 在数百年前被写回拼写，旧读音却被保留下来；作家们随后把这个名词扩展到一般意义上的谴责。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same saying-root plus its most confusing spelling cousin; the second holds the accusing words it is often mixed with.
note.cn: 第一组收「说」词根上的同族词，外加最容易混淆的拼写兄弟 indite；第二组收常与本词混用的控告类词。

entries.definition: showing or suggesting what something is like
entries.definitionCN: 同根，义为「指示的；表明……的」，注意第二个音节读短音 i，起诉义词则读长音 ai

entries.definition: to write or compose, a now archaic word
entries.definitionCN: 同源古词，义为「书写、创作」，与本词读音几乎相同却意义不同，且绝不带犯罪含义

entries.definition: the decision a court reaches or a considered judgement
entries.definitionCN: 同「说」词根，义为「裁决；定论」，与起诉相对，是审理的终点

entries.definition: an official accusation that someone has committed a crime
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「指控；罪名」，比 indictment 宽泛，不限于重罪，也不限于大陪审团程序

entries.definition: a claim that someone has done wrong
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「指责；控告」，可以是正式的，也可以是口头的、未必成立的

entries.definition: a court hearing where a person is formally told the charges
entries.definitionCN: 近义语场，义为「提审；传讯」，是起诉之后、被告被当庭告知罪名的那一步

normalIntro.en: Think of the silent c as the courtroom: it is written on the paper but never spoken aloud.
normalIntro.cn: 把那个不发音的 c 想成法庭本身：写在纸上，却从不说出口。

normal.en: The c in indictment is silent, exactly as it is in indict, so never say an extra k-sound.
normal.cn: indictment 里的 c 不发音，情况和 indict 一样，别多读出一个 k 音。

normal.en: The base verb is indict, the noun adds -ment; do not confuse it with indite, the old word for write.
normal.cn: 基础动词是 indict，名词加 -ment；别和旧词 indite（书写）混为一谈。

normal.en: Write it as one word, indict plus ment, and say it as in DITE, never as in DICT.
normal.cn: 拼写要连成一个词：indict 加 ment；读音要像「dite」，绝不像「dict」。

normal.en: The ending -ment is what turns the act of charging into both the charge and the document.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 正是把「提出指控」这个动作变成罪名或起诉书的东西。

normal.en: In essays a damning indictment of something is a favourite way to name a social failure.
normal.cn: 作文里用 a damning indictment of 是给社会问题下判语的常用说法。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk reading names aloud from a stiff sheet while the accused slowly lowers his head.
abstract.cn: 想象书记员捧着一页硬纸板文件大声念名字，被告慢慢低下头。

abstract.en: See the silent c standing like a guard who never speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象那个不发音的 c 像一名从不开口的守卫站在那里。

abstract.en: Think of a child leaving a school because it has no roof, and the empty building itself filing a complaint.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子因为校舍没有屋顶而离开学校，那座空楼本身就像在递交一纸控诉。

examples.en: The grand jury returned an indictment within a week.
examples.cn: 大陪审团在一周内作出了起诉。

examples.en: Her silence in court spoke louder than any indictment.
examples.cn: 她在法庭上的沉默比任何起诉都更响亮。

examples.en: The long waiting lists are a sharp indictment of the health service.
examples.cn: 长长的候诊名单是对医疗服务体系的尖锐控诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「认得门的」——检察官递上一纸文书，让被告认得法院的门，就是起诉；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 dicere「说、宣称」→ indicere「宣告、通知（含指控）」→ 分词 indictus → 中世纪法律拉丁语 indictare「在案卷上正式宣告指控」→ 法语 enditer/inditer → 英语 indict / indictment；-ment 为名词后缀。拼写的 c 来自拉丁语，读音却是古法语的样子，所以不发音。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the act of stating a formal charge, turns into the paper that states it, then spreads outward to any public condemnation and to the position of the person charged.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先从「正式陈述一项指控」这个动作出发，转而指陈述它的那张纸，随后向外扩散为任何公开的谴责，以及被控告者所处的处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of accusations read aloud in a hall while the accused lowers his head.
core.cn: 核心意象：大厅里有人宣读一页罪状，被念到名字的人低下头。

branches.en: The formal charge is the legal heart of the word.
branches.cn: 正式的指控是这个词的法律核心。

branches.en: The paper on which the charge is written is the everyday news sense.
branches.cn: 写着指控的那份文书是新闻里最常出现的义项。

branches.en: Outside the court, any exposed wrong becomes a condemnation.
branches.cn: 离开法庭之后，任何被揭露的问题都成了一种谴责。

branches.en: The person under the charge lives in its shadow until the case ends.
branches.cn: 被控告者在案件结束前都生活在这道阴影里。

branches.en: Legal and figurative accusations share the same accusing voice, only the setting changes.
branches.cn: 法律上的起诉与比喻性的谴责共用同一种指控口吻，变的只是场合。

intro.en: The word is honest Latin plus a French ending: a pointing prefix, a saying-stem, a law-French wrap, and the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: 这个词是诚实的拉丁语加外层的法语词尾：方向前缀、「说」的词干、一层法制法语外衣，最后是名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- points at a person, dicere says, and the -tus participle shapes the past; the -ment at the end is a later French gift.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 指向某人，dicere 表示说，分词词尾 -tus 构成过去；末尾的 -ment 则是后来法语给的。

items.example: Here the prefix points a statement at a person, not a negative.
items.exampleCN: 这里的前缀是把陈述对准某个人，而不是否定。

items.example: The verb is the saying-core of dictate, verdict and this word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 dictate、verdict 与本词共同的「说」的核心。

items.example: The verb widened from announcing in general to announcing a charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词从一般意义上的宣告，扩展到宣告一项指控。

items.example: The participle explains the silent c kept in the English spelling.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词说明了英语拼写中为何保留不发音的 c。

items.meaning: to accuse formally on the record
items.example: The law version of the verb narrowed it to the court.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词的法律版本把它收窄到法庭之内。

items.example: The noun suffix turns the base verb into the act and the document.
items.exampleCN: 名词后缀把基础动词变成动作，也变成那份文书。

items.meaning: to charge with a crime formally
items.example: The English verb keeps the silent c and the legal force.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词保留着不发音的 c，也保留着法律力量。

items.example: Adding -able marks what the law allows to be charged.
items.exampleCN: 加 -able 表示法律上允许被起诉的情况。

items.example: The prefix again yields reindictment, a fresh charge.
items.exampleCN: 再加 re- 得到 reindictment，即重新起诉。

items.meaning: to write or compose, now archaic
items.example: Indite and indict grew from the same French root but no longer mean the same.
items.exampleCN: indite 与 indict 出自同一法语词根，但如今已不同义。

definition_zh: 愤愤不平的；义愤的；感到受了委屈或不公的
definition_en: angry because something seems wrong, unfair, or insulting to you
core_image: 一个人被当众冤枉，脸涨得通红、眉头紧锁，想说又觉得说什么都没用
scene: 新来的员工被当众指责拿走了别人的东西，她涨红了脸，忍不住出声反驳。The young nurse felt indignant when she was told she had stolen the drugs.
sceneCN: 这里 indignant 是「愤愤不平的、义愤的」（第 1 个义项：觉得某事不公或受了委屈而愤怒）；句意：当有人告诉她那些药是她偷的时，这位年轻护士感到愤怒不平。

pos.zh: 愤愤不平的；义愤的；感到受了不公的

derivatives.zh: 由 indignant 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愤愤不平地；气愤地」
由 indignant 的词干加后缀 -ation 构成，义为「义愤；愤慨」，是这种情绪的名词形式
与 indignant 同出拉丁语 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的），义为「侮辱；使人蒙辱」，指引发愤慨的那种处境或待遇

senses.title: Angry at something unfair
senses.definition: feeling angry and resentful because something seems unjust, unfair, or insulting to you or to someone you care about
senses.definitionCN: 因为觉得某事不公正、不公平或受了侮辱而感到愤怒和不满，常用于自己或自己关心的人
senses.example: The residents were indignant about the sudden rise in fares.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们对车费突然上涨感到愤愤不平。
senses.why: The Latin dignus means worthy, and in- denies it, so indignation is the refusal to accept that someone is unworthy of fair treatment.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dignus 意为「值得的」，前缀 in- 表否定，所以义愤的根源就是「某人不该被这样对待」，拒绝承认对方「不值得被公平对待」。

senses.title: Insulted and hurt in pride
senses.definition: showing anger because you feel personally insulted or treated without respect
senses.definitionCN: 因为觉得自己受到侮辱或没被尊重而显出愤怒
senses.example: He gave an indignant snort when the waiter ignored him.
senses.exampleCN: 服务员没理他时，他气愤地哼了一声。
senses.why: Since dignus also means deserving of respect, having respect withdrawn is read as an insult, so the anger turns personal and proud.
senses.whyCN: dignus 也指「值得被尊重」，一旦不被尊重就被读成受辱，所以这种愤怒带上了个人化和自尊心的色彩。

senses.title: Expressed as protest
senses.titleCN: 以抗议、质问的方式表露
senses.definition: used of letters, speeches, or remarks that openly denounce a wrong
senses.definitionCN: 用于书信、言论或质问中公开谴责某种不公
senses.example: The newspaper received dozens of indignant letters about the verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 报社收到几十封对判决表示愤慨的来信。
senses.why: Anger at injustice seeks a witness, so the feeling hardens into a public complaint.
senses.whyCN: 面对不公的愤怒需要一个见证者，于是这种情绪固化为公开的抗议表达。

senses.title: Self-righteous edge
senses.definition: applied critically to anger that assumes the angry person is morally blameless
senses.definitionCN: 带批评色彩，指那种先假定自己道德上无辜、理直气壮的愤怒
senses.example: Her indignant tone suggested she had never done anything wrong herself.
senses.exampleCN: 她那愤愤不平的语气仿佛自己从未做错过任何事。
senses.why: The moral claim inside the word can be borrowed as a pose, so the same anger is sometimes mocked as self-righteous.
senses.whyCN: 这个词内含的道德主张可以被借作一种姿态，所以同样的愤怒有时会被讥为「自以为是的义愤」。

intro.en: Indignant comes from Latin indignari, to regard as unworthy, which is built on in-, not, and dignus, worthy.
intro.cn: indignant 来自拉丁语 indignari（认为不值得、愤慨），由 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的）构成。

items.en: Dignus means worthy, deserving, or of good standing.
items.cn: dignus 意为「值得的、应得的」，也指身份体面。

items.en: Indignus adds the negative prefix and means unworthy, from which indignari, to be angry at unfair treatment, is formed.
items.cn: indignus 加否定前缀，意为「不值得的」；由此构成 indignari，指对不公待遇感到愤慨。

items.en: The present participle indignans describes someone in the very act of being angry at a wrong.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语的现在分词 indignans 直接描写「正为不公而愤怒」的人。

items.en: Medieval French carries the adjective indigné, moving the shape closer to the modern word.
items.cn: 中世纪法语传入形容词 indigné，外形更接近现代形式。

items.en: Indignant enters English as an adjective meaning feeling scornful or angry, in the manner of Latin dignus and Latin indignus.
items.cn: 十六世纪后期 indignant 进入英语，表示「感到轻蔑、愤怒的」，沿用 dignity 与 indignity 同一个拉丁词根。

items.en: Today the word is most at home in news reporting about injustice, with the adverb form indignant plus -ly close behind.
items.cn: 今天它最常出现在报道不公的新闻中，由其加 -ly 构成的相关副词形式也随之常用。

note.en: Indignant is an adjective with a strong sense of injustice; its look-alikes share the Latin dignus root, while its near meanings shade from general anger to outrage.
note.cn: indignant 是带强烈「不公感」的形容词；形近词共享拉丁语 dignus 词根，近义词则从普通的生气到极度的义愤。

entries.definition: anger caused by something unfair or insulting
entries.definitionCN: 义愤；愤慨（同根名词，是 indignant 的情绪形式）

entries.definition: something that makes a person feel ashamed and humiliated
entries.definitionCN: 侮辱；使人蒙羞的处境（同根名词，但与 indignant 的义场不同）

entries.definition: the calm, serious quality of deserving respect
entries.definitionCN: 尊严；庄重（同一词根的正面形式，没有否定前缀）

entries.definition: feeling strong displeasure
entries.definitionCN: 生气的（范围更广，不一定含不公感）

entries.definition: extremely angry and shocked by cruelty or unfairness
entries.definitionCN: 义愤填膺的；震怒的（程度比 indignant 更强烈）

entries.definition: full of bitterness about unfair treatment
entries.definitionCN: 心怀怨恨的（更强调久久不平的怨气）

normalIntro.en: Indignant is the Latin dignus, worthy, with in- in front of it: a person who says the others are not worthy of treating me this way.
normalIntro.cn: indignant 就是拉丁语 dignus（值得的）前面加 in-：一个人觉得对方「不配这样对我」。

normal.en: Indignant shares its root with dignity and indignity.
normal.cn: indignant 与 dignity、indignity 同根。

normal.en: The adjective people rarely compare it, and the form more indignant is used when needed.
normal.cn: 这个形容词很少用比较级，需要时写成 more indignant。

normal.en: The common patterns are indignant at something and indignant about something.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 indignant at 某件事和 indignant about 某件事。

normal.en: The adverb indignant plus -ly tells how someone spoke or wrote.
normal.cn: 副词形式由 indignant 加 ly 构成，用来说明某人说话或写信的语气。

normal.en: Compare angry: angry is plain feeling, indignant adds the claim that a rule was broken.
normal.cn: 对比 angry：angry 只是情绪，indignant 还额外包含「有人违反了规矩」的判断。

abstract.en: See a hand pointing at a broken promise while the face turns red.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手直直指着被毁掉的承诺，脸同时涨得通红。

abstract.en: See a receipt being slapped on a desk, louder than any sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被拍在桌上，声音比任何一句话都响。

abstract.en: See a small note with a firm refusal signed at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小纸条，末尾签上名字，写着一句坚决的拒绝。

examples.en: She was indignant when the landlord kept her deposit without any reason.
examples.cn: 房东毫无理由扣下押金时，她愤愤不平。

examples.en: Several indignant parents wrote to the school about the new rule.
examples.cn: 几位愤慨的家长就新规定致信学校。

examples.en: He answered in an indignant voice that he had never been late.
examples.cn: 他气愤地回答说自己从未迟到过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因的哥难听」——因为的哥说的话太难听，乘客气得涨红了脸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的）→ indignari（认为不值得、义愤）→ 现在分词 indignans → 古法语 indigné → 英语 indignant，核心义「觉得对方不配」。

sensesIntro.en: Indignant begins with anger at injustice, passes into wounded pride at being treated without respect, hardens into public protest, and can finally be criticised as self-righteous.
sensesIntro.cn: indignant 先指面对不公时的愤怒，延伸到被迫失去尊重时的恼怒，再固化为公开的抗议，最后也可能被批评为「自以为是的义愤」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose face turns red because the others have judged them unworthy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人因为被别人看成「不配」而涨红了脸。

branches.en: Anger at something plainly unfair is the central sense.
branches.cn: 对明显不公的事感到愤怒是核心义项。

branches.en: Insulted pride narrows the anger to the person who feels disrespected.
branches.cn: 受辱的恼火把愤怒收拢到那个觉得不被尊重的人身上。

branches.en: Public protest turns the private feeling into letters, speeches, and outcry.
branches.cn: 公开抗议把私人情绪变成信件、演说和声讨。

branches.en: The self-righteous sense is the critical reading of the same moral claim.
branches.cn: 自以为是的义愤是对同一个道德主张的批判性解读。

branches.en: All three keep the image of someone who will not accept being called unworthy.
branches.cn: 三个义项都保留了「拒绝被说成不配」的画面。

intro.en: Indignant is built from the Latin negative prefix in- plus dignus, worthy, and its English family includes dignity, indignity, indignation, and indignantly.
intro.cn: indignant 由拉丁语否定前缀 in- 加 dignus（值得的）构成，英语词族包括 dignity、indignity、indignation、indignantly。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, dignus means worthy; with in- it becomes indignus, unworthy, and the verb indignari means to be angry at being treated as unworthy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中 dignus 意为「值得的」，加 in- 成为 indignus（不值得的），动词 indignari 意为对被视为「不配」而愤怒。

items.example: The prefix in- turns worthy into unworthy.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把「值得的」变成「不值得的」。

items.example: Dignus supplies the idea of what one deserves.
items.exampleCN: dignus 提供「应得之物」这一观念。

items.example: Indignus describes a treatment that is not deserved.
items.exampleCN: indignus 描述不应得的待遇。

items.example: Indignari is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: indignari 是形容词背后的动词。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ant forms indignant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 indignant。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms indignantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 indignantly。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms indignation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 indignation。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffixes -ity and -itas link dignity and indignity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 与拉丁语 -itas 把 dignity 和 indignity 联系起来。

items.example: Dignity keeps the root without the negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: dignity 保留词根而不带否定前缀。

items.example: Indignity adds the negative prefix to dignity.
items.exampleCN: indignity 在 dignity 前加上否定前缀。

definition_zh: 义愤；愤慨；因不公或受辱而生的愤怒
definition_en: anger that is caused by something you think is unfair, wrong, or insulting
core_image: 一群人围在公告栏前，看见被改动的名单，脸色骤变、声音升高
scene: 校方没做任何调查就取消了那名学生的奖学金，消息传开，整栋宿舍楼的学生都愤怒了。News of the cancelled scholarship filled the dormitory with indignation.
sceneCN: 这里 indignation 是「义愤、愤慨」（第 1 个义项：因不公或受辱而生的强烈愤怒）；句意：奖学金被取消的消息让整栋宿舍楼充满了愤慨。

pos.zh: 义愤；愤慨；因不公而生的愤怒

derivatives.zh: 由 indignation 的词干去掉 -ation 加 -ant 构成，义为「愤愤不平的；义愤的」，是这种情绪在个人身上的形容词形式
由 indignant 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愤然；气愤地」，用于描述说话或举动的方式
与 indignation 同出拉丁语 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的），义为「侮辱；使人蒙辱的待遇」，指能够激起义愤的那种处境

senses.title: Anger at unfairness
senses.definition: a strong feeling of anger and disapproval that something is unfair or wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因某事不公平或错误而产生的强烈愤怒与不认同
senses.example: The decision to close the library aroused widespread indignation.
senses.exampleCN: 关闭图书馆的决定激起了广泛的愤慨。
senses.why: Latin dignus means worthy and in- denies it, so the emotion is a protest against someone being treated as unworthy of fairness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dignus 意为「值得的」、in- 表否定，所以这种情绪本质上是对「某人被当成不配得到公平」的抗议。

senses.title: Shared public anger
senses.definition: the anger of a whole group or society, especially when reported in the news
senses.definitionCN: 一整群人或整个社会的愤怒，尤其见于新闻报道
senses.example: Public indignation forced the council to postpone the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 公众的愤慨迫使议会推迟了这次出售。
senses.why: An unjust act is witnessed by many at once, so one person feeling wronged quickly becomes a crowd feeling wronged.
senses.whyCN: 不公之举往往被许多人同时目睹，于是「一个人觉得委屈」迅速变成「一群人共同愤慨」。

senses.title: Haughty contempt
senses.definition: an older and literary use for proud scorn felt toward something beneath one
senses.definitionCN: 较古老且偏文学化的用法，指对不如自己之物抱有的傲慢轻蔑
senses.example: She looked at the cheap imitation with quiet indignation.
senses.exampleCN: 她以一种居高临下的轻蔑看着那件廉价的仿制品。
senses.why: The same refusal to accept something as worthy can turn outward as scorn for what one judges beneath oneself.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「不承认对方值得」，也可以翻转成向外指向的轻蔑——把对方判定为低劣之物。

senses.title: Self-righteous pose
senses.definition: a critical use for indignation put on to advertise ones own virtue
senses.definitionCN: 带批评色彩的用法，指为了让别人看见自己道德清白而装出来的愤慨
senses.example: His indignation over the budget looked practised rather than felt.
senses.exampleCN: 他对预算的愤慨看起来像是练熟的表演，而不是真感受。
senses.why: Because the word already carries a moral verdict, it can be borrowed as a costume by people more eager to look good than to set things right.
senses.whyCN: 这个词自带道德裁决，所以容易被只想显得正直、而不真想纠正问题的人借去当一件戏服。

intro.en: Indignation comes from Latin indignatio, built on in-, not, plus dignus, worthy, and passed through French into English.
intro.cn: indignation 来自拉丁语 indignatio，由 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Dignus means worthy, and indignus means unworthy or undeserved.
items.cn: dignus 意为「值得的」，indignus 意为「不值得的、不应得的」。

items.en: Indignatio names the feeling of anger at something unworthy, with a clear moral judgement inside it.
items.cn: indignatio 指因某事「不值得」而生的愤怒，情绪里自带道德判断。

items.en: Roman orators treat indignatio as a figure of speech that stirs a crowd by naming injustice.
items.cn: 古典拉丁修辞学把 indignatio 视为一种修辞手段，通过点明不公来煽动听众的情绪。

items.en: Old French indignacion hands the noun to Middle English with its moral colour intact.
items.cn: 古法语 indignacion 把这一名词传给中古英语，道德色彩完整保留。

items.en: The noun settles into English as the standard word for moral anger.
items.cn: 中古英语中，这个词固定为表示「道德愤怒」的标准词。

items.en: Today it appears most often in political and journalistic English, in phrases such as public indignation.
items.cn: 今天的英语中它多见于政治与新闻语境，常出现在 public indignation 这样的搭配里。

note.en: Indignation is the noun of moral anger; its look-alikes share the Latin dignus root, while its near meanings move from plain anger to outrage and scorn.
note.cn: indignation 是「道德愤怒」的名词；形近词共享拉丁语 dignus 词根，近义词则从普通的生气到震怒与轻蔑。

entries.definition: feeling angry at unfairness
entries.definitionCN: 愤愤不平的；义愤的（同根形容词，描述个人的感受）

entries.definition: an insult that makes a person lose dignity
entries.definitionCN: 侮辱；使人蒙辱的待遇（同根名词，指引发义愤的具体处境）

entries.definition: the quality of deserving respect
entries.definitionCN: 尊严；体面（同一词根的正面形式）

entries.definition: the general feeling of being displeased and hostile
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒（最宽泛的同类词，不一定涉及不公）

entries.definition: furious anger at something unacceptable
entries.definitionCN: 震怒；义愤（程度更强，常用于丑闻）

entries.definition: contempt for someone seen as worthless
entries.definitionCN: 轻蔑；鄙视（与 indignation 的古老轻蔑义相近）

normalIntro.en: Indignation is the noun behind indignant: Latin in-, not, plus dignus, worthy, plus the noun suffix -ation.
normalIntro.cn: indignation 是 indignant 的名词形式：拉丁语 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的）+ 名词后缀 -ation。

normal.en: Indignation and indignant are the noun and adjective of the same feeling.
normal.cn: indignation 与 indignant 是同一种情绪的名词和形容词形式。

normal.en: Latin roots return in public indignation, which news writing loves.
normal.cn: 新闻写作偏爱 public indignation 这样的搭配，拉丁词根在此重现。

normal.en: People arouse, express, or feel indignation, rarely do it.
normal.cn: 人们用 arouse、express、feel 跟 indignation 搭配，很少用 do。

normal.en: With indignation is the standard phrase for refusing with a moral voice.
normal.cn: with indignation 是「带着道德口吻拒绝」的标准搭配。

normal.en: Compare outrage: outrage is louder and often about a scandal, indignation is calmer and more principled.
normal.cn: 对比 outrage：outrage 更响亮、多与丑闻相连，indignation 更克制、更讲道理。

abstract.en: See a crowd reading the same notice and all raising their voices at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人读着同一张告示，同时提高嗓门。

abstract.en: See a letter read aloud in a meeting room, the paper shaking slightly.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信念到一半，纸在手上微微发抖。

abstract.en: See a moral scale tipping hard to one side while the crowd watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆道德天平在众人注视下猛地倒向一边。

examples.en: There was widespread indignation at the size of the bonuses.
examples.cn: 奖金数额之高引起了广泛的愤慨。

examples.en: She spoke with real indignation about the way the workers had been treated.
examples.cn: 她谈起工人们所受的对待时，语气中满是真正的义愤。

examples.en: The report provoked indignation among parents and teachers alike.
examples.cn: 这份报告在家长和教师中同样激起了愤慨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因的哥们审」——因为的哥们被审得不公平，围观的人都气愤起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的）→ indignatio（义愤）→ 古法语 indignacion → 中古英语 indignation，核心义「认定不公而生的愤怒」。

sensesIntro.en: Indignation starts as anger at unfairness, spreads to whole crowds in public life, keeps an older literary sense of proud scorn, and can finally be mocked as a pose.
sensesIntro.cn: indignation 先指因不公而生的愤怒，扩展到公众层面的集体愤慨，还保留着高傲轻蔑的旧文学义，最后也可能被讥为「装出来的义愤」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group whose faces change when they see a list that has been tampered with.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人看到被人动过手脚的名单，脸色骤然一变。

branches.en: Personal anger at unfairness is the central sense.
branches.cn: 个人因不公而生的愤怒是核心义项。

branches.en: Shared public anger widens the feeling to groups and society.
branches.cn: 公众集体愤慨把这种情绪扩展到群体与社会。

branches.en: Haughty contempt keeps the oldest literary layer of the word.
branches.cn: 居高临下的轻蔑保留了这个词最古老的文学层次。

branches.en: The self-righteous pose is the sceptical reading of the same moral voice.
branches.cn: 装出来的义愤是对同一种道德口吻的怀疑式解读。

branches.en: All three rest on the judgement that something was not worth what it got.
branches.cn: 三个义项都建立在「某事不配得到它所受的对待」这一判断上。

intro.en: Indignation is the abstract noun built on the Latin stem dignus, worthy, with the negative prefix in- and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: indignation 是建立在拉丁词干 dignus（值得的）上的抽象名词，加上否定前缀 in- 和名词后缀 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin indignatio is formed from indignus, unworthy, which is in-, not, plus dignus, worthy; the abstract noun -atio names the feeling itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 indignatio 由 indignus（不值得的）派生，而 indignus 是 in-（不）+ dignus（值得的）；抽象名词后缀 -atio 指这种情绪本身。

items.example: The prefix in- marks the absence of worth.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 标示「价值」的缺失。

items.example: Dignus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: dignus 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Indignus supplies the moral verdict.
items.exampleCN: indignus 提供道德判断。

items.example: Indignatio names the emotion itself.
items.exampleCN: indignatio 直接指这种情绪。

items.meaning: action or state, forming abstract nouns
items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态，构成抽象名词
items.example: The suffix -ation forms indignation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 indignation。

items.example: The suffix -ant gives the adjective indignant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 给出形容词 indignant。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms indignantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 indignantly。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms dignity and indignity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 dignity 与 indignity。

items.example: Indignation keeps the Latin noun sense.
items.exampleCN: indignation 保留了拉丁语名词的含义。

definition_zh: 侮辱；屈辱；使人丧失尊严的待遇；有损体面的处境
definition_en: a situation or treatment that makes you feel ashamed, humiliated, or without dignity
core_image: 一位老人排队很久，却被叫到一旁当众掏遍口袋接受检查
scene: 那位老人只是想领一份免费的午餐，却被要求当众打开包、报出全部家底。The old man had to empty his pockets in front of the clerk, an indignity he had never expected.
sceneCN: 这里 indignity 是「侮辱、使人丧失尊严的待遇」（第 1 个义项：被当作没有尊严的人来对待的具体处境）；句意：老人不得不在职员面前把口袋掏空，这是他从未料想过的屈辱。

pos.zh: 侮辱；屈辱；有损尊严的待遇

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根 in- + dignus 派生，加后缀 -ant 构成，义为「愤愤不平的」；注意 indignant 说的是感到不公的人，indignity 说的是使人丢脸的事
由同一词根加后缀 -ation 构成，义为「义愤」，是 indignity 所引发的情绪
去掉否定前缀 in- 的正面形式，义为「尊严；庄重」，indignity 正是尊严被剥掉的处境
由 dignity 派生的形容词，义为「有尊严的；庄重的」，与 indignity 构成意义反照

senses.title: Humiliating treatment
senses.definition: a situation or treatment that makes you feel foolish, ashamed, or without respect
senses.definitionCN: 使人觉得自己愚蠢、羞愧或不受尊重的处境或待遇
senses.example: The passengers suffered the indignity of being searched twice.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客们遭受了被搜查两次的屈辱。
senses.why: Latin dignitas is the worth a person carries, and in- takes it away, so an indignity is any situation that strips that worth in public.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dignitas 指一个人身上「该被尊重的分量」，前缀 in- 把它拿走，所以侮辱就是任何当众剥掉这份分量的处境。

senses.title: Loss of status
senses.definition: the loss of the position or standing that a person once enjoyed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人曾经拥有的地位或体面被剥夺
senses.example: He endured years of indignity as a former officer taking orders from juniors.
senses.exampleCN: 作为昔日的军官，他多年忍受着听命于下级的屈辱。
senses.why: Because dignitas also meant rank and office, losing rank is experienced as losing an outward badge of worth.
senses.whyCN: 因为 dignitas 也有「官阶、职位」之义，失去身份地位就被体验为失去了价值的外在徽章。

senses.title: A humiliating act
senses.definition: a particular action or episode that humiliates someone, often counted as one among many
senses.definitionCN: 某一次具体的、使人蒙羞的行为或事件，常以多起计
senses.example: The meal of cold soup and hard bread was yet another indignity for the prisoners.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿冷汤硬面包又是一桩让囚犯们蒙羞的事。
senses.why: Any single event can perform the stripping of dignity, so the word also marks one countable incident rather than a state.
senses.whyCN: 任何单个事件都可能完成「剥掉尊严」的动作，所以这个词也用来指望得出的单次事件，而不只是一种状态。

senses.title: Proud refusal of an insult
senses.definition: a rare and literary sense for scorn or for the proud refusal to accept something seen as beneath ones dignity
senses.definitionCN: 较罕见且文学化的用法，指轻蔑，或高傲地拒绝接受有失体面的事物
senses.example: She regarded the offer with the indignity of one who finds money vulgar.
senses.exampleCN: 她像一位视金钱为粗俗的人那样，带着不屑看待这个提议。
senses.why: A person who refuses to be made unworthy may turn the same idea outward and look down on what others accept.
senses.whyCN: 一个拒绝被别人看轻的人，也可以把这个念头转向外面，反过来轻视别人接受的东西。

intro.en: Indignity comes from Latin indignitas, the state of being unworthy, built on in-, not, plus dignitas, worth or rank.
intro.cn: indignity 来自拉丁语 indignitas（「不值得」的状态），由 in-（不）+ dignitas（价值、身份）构成。

items.en: Dignus means worthy, and dignitas means worth, standing, or rank.
items.cn: dignus 意为「值得的」，dignitas 意为「价值、身份、官阶」。

items.en: Indignitas is the condition of lacking worth or being treated without respect.
items.cn: indignitas 指缺乏价值、不被以尊重相待的状态。

items.en: Late Latin usage shifts from a quality of a thing to a treatment carried out against a person.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的用法从「事物的劣质」转向「对人施加的待遇」。

items.en: Old French indignité passes the noun toward English with the sense of shame and insult.
items.cn: 古法语 indignité 把这一名词传给英语，带上了「羞耻、侮辱」之义。

items.en: Middle English indignite names a lack of honour and the act that causes it.
items.cn: 中古英语中 indignite 既指荣誉的缺失，也指造成这种缺失的行为。

items.en: Today the word is common in the plural, as in a series of indignities, and often appears with suffer.
items.cn: 今天这个词常以复数出现，如 a series of indignities，并常与 suffer 搭配。

note.en: Indignity is the dignus family noun for being treated as worthless; its look-alikes include dignity and indignant, and its near meanings run from humiliation to loss of face.
note.cn: indignity 是 dignus 词族中标示「被当作一无是处的人对待」的名词；形近词有 dignity、indignant，近义词则从羞辱到丢脸不等。

entries.definition: the quality of deserving and showing respect
entries.definitionCN: 尊严；庄重（去掉否定前缀的正面形式，意义与 indignity 相对）

entries.definition: angry at unfairness
entries.definitionCN: 愤愤不平的（同根形容词，描述受害者的情绪而非处境）

entries.definition: anger at unfairness
entries.definitionCN: 义愤（同根名词，指情绪，而 indignity 指事件或待遇）

entries.definition: the feeling of being made to look foolish or worthless
entries.definitionCN: 羞辱；丢脸（更强调心理上的羞耻感）

entries.definition: something rude that offends a person on purpose
entries.definitionCN: 侮辱；辱骂（多指言语或举动，恶意的程度更明显）

entries.definition: the loss of other peoples respect
entries.definitionCN: 丢脸；失宠（侧重名声上的失礼，常因自身过错）

normalIntro.en: Indignity is dignity with a negative prefix: Latin in-, not, plus dignitas, worth and rank, so it is worth taken away from a person.
normalIntro.cn: indignity 是加了否定前缀的 dignity：拉丁语 in-（不）+ dignitas（价值与身份），即「一个人的价值被拿走」。

normal.en: Indignity takes its plural regularly as indignities.
normal.cn: indignity 的复数按规则变形为 indignities。

normal.en: The common verb is suffer, and the common pattern is suffer the indignity of doing something.
normal.cn: 最常用的动词是 suffer，常见结构是 suffer the indignity of 加动名词。

normal.en: The noun is countable: one indignity, several indignities.
normal.cn: 这个名词可数：一件屈辱、多处屈辱。

normal.en: Keep indignant for the angry person and indignity for the humiliating event.
normal.cn: 记住 indignant 描述愤怒的人，indignity 描述使人屈辱的事。

normal.en: Cicero uses indignitas in Latin for unworthiness and meanness of character, showing how old the family is.
normal.cn: 西塞罗时代拉丁语已用 indignitas 表示「无价值、品格卑劣」，可见这个词族之古老。

abstract.en: See a jacket with all its pockets turned inside out at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套的口袋同时被翻过来，露出空空的里子。

abstract.en: See a chair pushed into the corner of a crowded room where a person must sit alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张椅子被推到拥挤房间的角落，那个人只能独自坐着。

abstract.en: See a badge being unpinned from a uniform and handed to someone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚徽章从制服上被摘下，交到别人手里。

examples.en: Being made to queue in the rain was an indignity he would not forget.
examples.cn: 被逼在雨里排队是他不会忘记的一次屈辱。

examples.en: The new policy spared elderly patients the indignity of undressing for a scan.
examples.cn: 新规定免除了老年病人为做扫描而脱衣的屈辱。

examples.en: She accepted the indignities of the job because the pay was good.
examples.cn: 因为报酬不错，她接受了这份工作中的种种屈辱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in 第哥提」——被人从门口就拉着衣领「提」出来，当众丢尽脸面；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dignitas（价值；身份）→ indignitas（无价值；不体面的处境）→ 古法语 indignité → 中古英语 indignite → 英语 indignity，核心义「被剥掉尊严」。

sensesIntro.en: Indignity begins with humiliating treatment done to a person, widens to the loss of rank and standing over time, counts each separate humiliating act, and keeps an old literary sense of proud refusal.
sensesIntro.cn: indignity 先指被强加于人的屈辱待遇，扩展到地位的跌落与体面的丧失，也可以一件件计数，最后保留着高傲拒绝的旧文学义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing with every pocket turned out while others watch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在众目睽睽下把所有口袋翻空。

branches.en: Humiliating treatment is the central sense.
branches.cn: 屈辱的待遇是核心义项。

branches.en: Loss of status extends the stripping to rank and career.
branches.cn: 身份被贬把「剥掉」的过程扩展到地位与职业。

branches.en: A single humiliating act is the countable, episode sense.
branches.cn: 单次使人丢脸的事件是可行的计数式义项。

branches.en: Scornful refusal turns the same idea outward as pride.
branches.cn: 轻蔑地拒绝把这个念头转向外面，表现为骄傲。

branches.en: All three show worth being taken away, whether as treatment, rank, or one act.
branches.cn: 三个义项都呈现「价值被拿走」，只是或为待遇、或为地位、或为单次事件。

intro.en: Indignity sets the negative prefix in- against dignitas, worth; its English family includes dignity, dignified, indignant, and indignation.
intro.cn: indignity 用否定前缀 in- 与 dignitas（价值）对置；英语词族包括 dignity、dignified、indignant、indignation。

latinIntro.en: Latin dignitas means worth, standing, and honour; indignitas means the lack of it, and so the state of being put to shame.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dignitas 意为「价值、身份、荣誉」；indignitas 指缺乏这些，也就是被置于羞耻之中。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the worth behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定了这个词背后的价值。

items.example: Dignus is the root adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: dignus 是整个词族的词根形容词。

items.example: Dignitas supplies the idea of standing.
items.exampleCN: dignitas 提供「身份地位」这一观念。

items.example: Indignitas is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: indignitas 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms indignity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 indignity。

items.meaningCN: 以 y 结尾名词的复数词尾
items.example: The plural ending gives indignities.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾给出 indignities。

items.example: Dignity is indignity without the negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: dignity 就是去掉否定前缀后的对立词。

items.meaning: made or having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ified forms dignified from dignity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ified 使 dignity 派生出 dignified。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms indignant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 indignant。

definition_zh: 怠惰的；慵懒的；无所事事的；（医学）生长缓慢而无痛的
definition_en: disliking work or activity and preferring to rest, and in medicine slow to develop and causing little pain
core_image: 一个人躺在树荫下的长凳上，明知有事要做却不想抬起身子
scene: 老师看着趴在桌上打瞌睡的学生，摇头叹气。The teacher sighed at the indolent pupil who slept through the whole lesson.
sceneCN: 这里 indolent 是「怠惰的；懒惰不愿动」（第 1 个义项：不愿劳动、贪图安逸）；句意：老师对着那个整节课都在睡觉的懒学生叹气。

pos.zh: 怠惰的；慵懒的；无所事事的
（医学）生长缓慢的；无痛的

derivatives.zh: 由 indolent 去尾加后缀 -ence 构成，义为「懒惰；慵懒」
形容词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「懒洋洋地」
较少见的名词变体，加 -ency 构成，义同上，多见于早期英语

senses.title: Disliking work and activity
senses.definition: lazy and preferring rest to any effort
senses.definitionCN: 懒惰，宁肯歇着也不愿出力
senses.example: An indolent clerk can ruin the whole office.
senses.exampleCN: 一个懒散的职员能拖垮整个办公室。
senses.why: Latin in- means not and dolere means to feel pain, so the word pictures a person who does not want to suffer effort at all.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，dolere 表示「感到痛苦」，所以这个词画的是一点苦都不想吃的人。

senses.title: Moving slowly and lazily
senses.definition: showing a relaxed, slow, and unhurried manner
senses.definitionCN: 姿态放松、动作缓慢、不急不赶
senses.example: The cat lay indolent in the afternoon sun.
senses.exampleCN: 那只猫懒洋洋地躺在午后的阳光里。
senses.why: From refusing effort it is a short step to describing the calm, slow body language that goes with it.
senses.whyCN: 从拒绝费力只差一步，就用来形容随之而来的那份缓慢悠闲的神态。

senses.title: Sluggish and inactive by habit
senses.definition: habitually idle, especially when idleness causes harm
senses.definitionCN: 习惯性无所事事，尤其在这种懒散造成损害时
senses.example: The indolent government ignored the warnings for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个懈怠的政府多年来对警告置之不理。
senses.why: When idleness settles in as a character trait, the word becomes a moral judgement on habits rather than a passing mood.
senses.whyCN: 当懒散固化成性格特征时，这个词就从一时的状态变成对习惯的道德评判。

senses.title: Slow to develop and painless
senses.definition: used of wounds or growths that spread slowly and cause little pain
senses.definitionCN: 形容伤口或肿块扩散缓慢、几乎不引起疼痛
senses.example: The doctor described it as an indolent growth that needed watching.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说那是一个生长缓慢的肿块，需要观察。
senses.why: Medical writers reused the literal layers of the Latin root, slow and without pain, so the disease gives few painful clues.
senses.whyCN: 医学作者直接用了拉丁词根的字面义「缓慢」与「无痛」，所以这种病灶几乎不给人疼痛的提示。

intro.en: Indolent comes from Latin indolens, meaning without pain, after in-, not, and dolere, to feel pain.
intro.cn: indolent 来自拉丁语 indolens（无痛的），由 in-（不）与 dolere（感到痛苦）构成。

items.en: Dolere means to feel pain or to grieve.
items.cn: dolere 意为感到疼痛或悲伤。

items.en: Indolens means not feeling pain, or free from pain.
items.cn: indolens 意为感觉不到疼痛，或无痛的。

items.en: Writers extend the idea to anyone who avoids pain, including the effort of work.
items.cn: 后世作者把这一概念扩展到回避一切痛苦的人，包括劳作之苦。

items.en: English borrows the word in the sense of careless and lazy.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借用此词，义为「漫不经心的、懒惰的」。

items.en: Medicine uses indolent for slow and painless wounds or growths.
items.cn: 十九世纪的医学用 indolent 指生长缓慢、无痛的伤口或肿块。

items.en: The everyday sense is lazy, while the medical sense stays technical.
items.cn: 现代英语的日常义项是「懒惰」，医学义项仍属专业用法。

note.en: Indolent belongs to the dolere family of pain words, and it sits beside lazy, idle, and sluggish.
note.cn: indolent 属于以 dolere（疼痛）为核心的同族词，并与 lazy、idle、sluggish 意义相邻。

entries.definition: the habit of being lazy
entries.definitionCN: 慵懒；懒惰成性

entries.definition: in a lazy, relaxed way
entries.definitionCN: 懒洋洋地

entries.definition: an expression of sympathy after a death
entries.definitionCN: 哀悼；慰问（condole 由 dolere 加 com- 构成，义为「共同悲伤」）

entries.definition: unwilling to work or make an effort
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰的；不愿出力的

entries.definition: not working, or not doing anything useful
entries.definitionCN: 闲着的；无所事事的

entries.definition: slow and lacking energy
entries.definitionCN: 迟缓的；懒散的；反应慢的

normalIntro.en: Indolent is built from Latin for without pain, so it means a person who takes no pains and makes no effort.
normalIntro.cn: indolent 由拉丁语「无痛」构成，所以它指的是既不肯吃苦、也不肯出力的人。

normal.en: Indolence is the noun, and indolently is the adverb.
normal.cn: indolence 是名词，indolently 是副词。

normal.en: The adjective takes more and most for comparison.
normal.cn: 这个形容词用 more 和 most 构成比较级与最高级。

normal.en: Latin dolere means to feel pain, and it also gives condolence.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 dolere 意为感到痛苦，它也是 condolence 的来源。

normal.en: An indolent person stays seated when work appears.
normal.cn: indolent 的人一看见有活要干就坐着不动。

normal.en: Compare lazy: lazy is everyday, while indolent is more formal and literary.
normal.cn: 对比 lazy：lazy 更日常，indolent 更正式、更书面。

abstract.en: Picture a man who will not rise from a low bench because standing up might hurt.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人不肯从矮凳上起身，因为站起来也许要费点劲。

abstract.en: Imagine a heavy body still asleep while the sun is already high.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳都高高升起了，一个沉重的身体还在睡。

abstract.en: Think of a slowly spreading stain that never hurts at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一处慢慢扩散却毫无痛感的污渍。

examples.en: He grew indolent after retirement and rarely left the flat.
examples.cn: 退休之后他变得懒散，很少离开公寓。

examples.en: Her indolence cost the team a whole week of work.
examples.cn: 她的懒惰让团队白损失了整整一周的工作。

examples.en: The islanders led an indolent life beside the warm sea.
examples.cn: 岛民们在温暖的海边过着慵懒闲散的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印兜懒人」——印一张卡片塞进口袋里，这人就懒得再动弹。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dolere（感到痛苦）→ indolens（无痛的）→ 后世引申为「不愿受劳作之苦」→ 英语 indolent（懒惰的）；同族词还有 doleful、condolence。

sensesIntro.en: Indolent starts from the idea of feeling no pain, which becomes refusing effort, then a lazy manner, a fixed habit, and finally a medical description.
sensesIntro.cn: indolent 从「感觉不到痛」出发，引申为不愿费力，再成为慵懒的神态与固定的习性，最后成为医学上的描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who stays in the shade because work would cost effort.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人待在树荫里不肯动，因为干活太费劲。

branches.en: The everyday sense is simply unwillingness to work.
branches.cn: 最日常的义项就是不愿干活。

branches.en: The relaxed, slow manner is the visible picture of that refusal.
branches.cn: 慵懒缓慢的神态是那种拒绝的外在画面。

branches.en: As a habit the word turns into a judgement of character.
branches.cn: 当它固化为习惯，就变成对品性的评判。

branches.en: Medicine keeps the literal layers of slow and without pain.
branches.cn: 医学保留了「缓慢」与「无痛」这两层字面义。

branches.en: Both a lazy afternoon and a lazy government come from refusing effort.
branches.cn: 慵懒的午后与懈怠的政府都源于不愿费力。

intro.en: Indolent is a Latin negative prefix plus the pain verb dolere, with English indolence and indolently built on it.
intro.cn: indolent 由拉丁语否定前缀加表「疼痛」的 dolere 构成，英语围绕它形成 indolence 与 indolently。

latinIntro.en: Latin dolere means to feel pain, and its negative indolens means feeling none.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dolere 意为感到疼痛，其否定形式 indolens 意为感觉不到疼痛。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the pain verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定了这个表疼痛的动词。

items.example: Dolere supplies the pain image.
items.exampleCN: dolere 提供「疼痛」的意象。

items.example: Dolor is the noun of the same family.
items.exampleCN: dolor 是同族的拉丁名词。

items.example: Indolens is the direct source form.
items.exampleCN: indolens 是直接来源形式。

items.example: Indolence is the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: indolence 是抽象名词。

items.example: The suffix -ence forms indolence.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ence 构成 indolence。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms indolently.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 indolently。

items.example: Condole joins the same pain verb with a prefix meaning with.
items.exampleCN: condole 把同一个疼痛动词与表示「共同」的前缀结合在一起。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms doleful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 doleful。

definition_zh: 纵情于；沉溺于；纵容；迁就；满足（愿望）；（对兴趣）投入、放纵
definition_en: to let yourself or someone else enjoy something you want, often more than is good, or to allow yourself a particular interest
core_image: 宠孩子的大人把最后一块蛋糕又递给已经吃撑的孩子
scene: 度假的最后一天，他索性赖在沙滩上一整天，什么都不想管。On the last day of the holiday he decided to indulge himself and stay on the beach all morning.
sceneCN: 这里 indulge 是「纵情于；让自己尽情享受」（第 1 个义项：让自己或别人沉溺于所贪图的事）；句意：假期的最后一天，他决定放纵自己，整个上午都待在沙滩上。

pos.zh: 纵情于；沉溺于；满足（欲望）
纵容；迁就；溺爱
（对某事）着迷；投入（兴趣）

collocations.zh: 放纵自己；让自己享受一下
沉迷于爱好；尽情去做喜欢的事

derivatives.zh: 由 indulge 加后缀 -ence 构成，义为「放纵；纵容；沉迷之物」
由动词词干加 -ent 构成，义为「纵容的；溺爱的」
形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「宽容纵容地」

senses.title: To allow yourself a pleasure
senses.definition: to let yourself enjoy something you like, often a little too much
senses.definitionCN: 让自己享受喜欢的东西，常常有点过分
senses.example: She indulged in a long hot bath after work.
senses.exampleCN: 下班后她痛痛快快洗了个热水澡。
senses.why: The Latin sense was to be kind to someone, and turning that kindness on yourself gives the idea of giving in to your own desires.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「对人宽厚」，把这份宽厚转向自己，就成了顺从自己的欲望。

senses.title: To spoil someone by giving way
senses.definition: to let someone do or get what they want, sometimes with bad effects
senses.definitionCN: 让别人想做什么、想要什么都如愿，有时带来坏结果
senses.example: The grandparents indulge their grandson without limit.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父母无底线地溺爱孙子。
senses.why: Kindness given to another person without limits turns quickly into spoiling.
senses.whyCN: 对别人无底线的善意，很快就会变成溺爱与娇惯。

senses.title: To satisfy a wish or need
senses.definition: to allow a desire or need to be met
senses.definitionCN: 让某种愿望或需要得到满足
senses.example: He indulged a taste for old maps on the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 旅途中他满足了收集古地图的爱好。
senses.why: The object shifts from people to wishes and habits, so the verb simply names the act of satisfying them.
senses.whyCN: 宾语从人转向愿望与爱好，动词因此就表示让这些愿望得到满足。

senses.title: To take part in something with pleasure
senses.definition: to spend time on an interest or activity because you enjoy it
senses.definitionCN: 因为喜爱而把时间花在某个兴趣或活动上
senses.example: She indulges in painting for hours on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 周末她常常沉浸在画画里好几个小时。
senses.why: When the activity itself is the source of pleasure, the word loses any sense of blame and simply means giving time to it.
senses.whyCN: 当活动本身就是快乐的来源时，这个词的责备意味消失，只剩下「把时间交给它」。

intro.en: Indulge goes back to Latin indulgere, meaning to be kind, gracious, or yielding to someone.
intro.cn: indulge 可追溯到拉丁语 indulgere，意为「宽厚、仁惠，对某人让步」。

items.en: Indulgere means to be accommodating, kind, or to give in to someone.
items.cn: indulgere 意为待人宽厚、随和，或对某人让步。

items.en: The Church uses indulgentia for a remission of a penalty, the source of the English religious sense.
items.cn: 中世纪教会用 indulgentia 表示「免罚」，这是英语宗教义项「赦罪」的来源。

items.en: English borrows indulge with the sense of being kindly disposed towards someone.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语借入 indulge，义为「对某人心怀宽厚」。

items.en: The modern meaning of gratifying a desire or a person grows common.
items.cn: 「满足欲望、迁就某人」的现代含义开始流行。

items.en: To indulge oneself, or to indulge in something, becomes the everyday use.
items.cn: indulge oneself 与 indulge in something 成为最常见的日常用法。

note.en: Indulge shares its stem with indulgence and indulgent, and in meaning it lies close to spoil, pamper, and gratify.
note.cn: indulge 与 indulgence、indulgent 同词干，意义上贴近 spoil、pamper、gratify。

entries.definition: the act of allowing yourself too much pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 放纵；纵容；沉迷之物

entries.definition: giving way to others too easily
entries.definitionCN: 纵容的；溺爱的

entries.definition: allowed a pleasure in the past
entries.definitionCN: 纵容过；曾经沉溺（过去式或过去分词）

entries.definition: to harm someone by giving them everything they want
entries.definitionCN: 宠坏；惯坏

entries.definition: to treat someone with too much care and comfort
entries.definitionCN: 娇惯；过分呵护

entries.definition: to satisfy a desire or a wish
entries.definitionCN: 使满足；取悦（较正式）

normalIntro.en: Indulge is the verb behind indulgence and indulgent, and in practice it always points at pleasure or at someone you let go too far.
normalIntro.cn: indulge 是 indulgence 与 indulgent 背后的动词，实际用法总指向享乐，或指向被你放得太宽的人。

normal.en: The verb takes the endings -s, -ed, and -ing.
normal.cn: 这个动词分别加 -s、-ed 和 -ing。

normal.en: Indulge in something means enjoying it rather freely.
normal.cn: indulge in something 指相当放开地享受某事。

normal.en: Indulge oneself is a gentle way to say treat yourself.
normal.cn: indulge oneself 是「犒劳自己一下」的委婉说法。

normal.en: The noun is indulgence and the adjective is indulgent.
normal.cn: 名词是 indulgence，形容词是 indulgent。

normal.en: Compare spoil: spoil usually blames the result, while indulge only describes the act.
normal.cn: 对比 spoil：spoil 多半是在责怪结果，indulge 只描述这个行为。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a second cake towards a child who is already full.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把第二块蛋糕推给已经吃饱的孩子。

abstract.en: Imagine a soft door that opens for every request.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇柔软的门，每个请求一来它就开了。

abstract.en: Think of a wish list where every item quietly gets ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象一张愿望清单，每一项都被悄悄打了勾。

examples.en: Parents who indulge every demand raise children who cannot cope.
examples.cn: 对孩子有求必应的父母会养出无法应对挫折的孩子。

examples.en: On Friday nights she allows herself to indulge in a little chocolate.
examples.cn: 每逢周五晚上，她会允许自己吃一点巧克力放纵一下。

examples.en: He indulged his curiosity and read the whole archive.
examples.cn: 他顺从了自己的好奇心，把整批档案都读完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引大个」——引来了就给他最大的那块蛋糕，就是纵容。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 indulgere（宽厚待人；让步）→ 英语 indulge（纵容、沉溺）；同族词 indulgence 早年经教会拉丁语 indulgentia（免罚）传入，因此还带有「赦免」的旧义。

sensesIntro.en: Indulge moves from being kind to someone, to giving way to people, to satisfying wishes, and finally to enjoying an interest.
sensesIntro.cn: indulge 从「对人宽厚」出发，发展为对人让步与迁就，再到满足愿望，最后是沉浸于自己的爱好。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that keeps handing out what was asked for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手不停把别人要的东西递出去。

branches.en: Kindness turned on yourself becomes enjoying a pleasure.
branches.cn: 把宽厚转向自己，就是尽情享乐。

branches.en: Kindness without limits becomes spoiling another person.
